sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच । धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १-१ ॥
translation: Dhritarashtra said: -- On the field of Kurus, which promotes righteousness, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people (my sons) and the Pandavas who, eager for battle, had (there) met together.
itrans: dhR^itarAShTra uvAcha . dharmakShetre kurukShetre samavetA yuyutsavaH . mAmakAH pANDavAshchaiva kimakurvata sa~njaya .. 1-1 ..

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ १-२ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said :--Now the prince Duryodhana having seen the army of the Pandavas arrayed in battle order) approached his teacher (Drona) and spoke (these) words.
itrans: sa~njaya uvAcha . dR^iShTvA tu pANDavAnIkaM vyUDhaM duryodhanastadA . AchAryamupasa~Ngamya rAjA vachanamabravIt .. 1-2 ..

sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥ १-३ ॥
translation: Behold this mighty host of the sons of Pandu, O Acharya, which is arrayed by Drupada's son, thy intelligent pupil.
itrans: pashyaitAM pANDuputrANAmAchArya mahatI.n chamUm . vyUDhAM drupadaputreNa tava shiShyeNa dhImatA .. 1-3 ..

sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥ १-४ ॥
translation: Here (in the army) are heroes and great bowmen who are equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna, (to wit), Yuyudhana, Virata, Drupada, (all) of the great car, (i.e., great warriors);
itrans: atra shUrA maheShvAsA bhImArjunasamA yudhi . yuyudhAno virATashcha drupadashcha mahArathaH .. 1-4 ..

sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥ १-५ ॥
translation: Dhristaketu, Chekitana, the prince of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, Saibya, (who are all) men of prowess and foremost among men;
itrans: dhR^iShTaketushchekitAnaH kAshirAjashcha vIryavAn . purujitkuntibhojashcha shaibyashcha narapu~NgavaH .. 1-5 ..

sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥ १-६ ॥
translation: Yudhamanyu the victorious, Uttamaujas, the undaunted, Subhadra's son (Abhimanyu) and the sons of Draupadi, every one of them being a Maharatha.
itrans: yudhAmanyushcha vikrAnta uttamaujAshcha vIryavAn . saubhadro draupadeyAshcha sarva eva mahArathAH .. 1-6 ..

sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥ १-७ ॥
translation: Now on our side also (thou mayest) know those who are the best among the leaders of our army. I name them for your special notice.
itrans: asmAkaM tu vishiShTA ye tAnnibodha dvijottama . nAyakA mama sainyasya sa.nj~nArthaM tAnbravImi te .. 1-7 ..

sanskrit: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥ १-८ ॥
translation: “Thyself and Bhishma, and Karna, and Kripa the victorious in battle, Aswathama, and Vikarna ; so also (Bhurisravas) the son of Somadatta;”
itrans: bhavAnbhIShmashcha karNashcha kR^ipashcha samiti~njayaH . ashvatthAmA vikarNashcha saumadattistathaiva cha .. 1-8 ..

sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥ १-९ ॥
translation: “And many others (are) the warriors armed with diverse weapons and missiles, all dexterous in battle, that have renounced their life for my sake.”
itrans: anye cha bahavaH shUrA madarthe tyaktajIvitAH . nAnAshastrapraharaNAH sarve yuddhavishAradAH .. 1-9 ..

sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥ १-१० ॥
translation: Such (as it is), insufficient seems the strength (army) carefully looked after by Bhishma; but sufficient does this army of theirs appear, which is ably led by Bhima.”
itrans: aparyAptaM tadasmAkaM balaM bhIShmAbhirakShitam . paryApta.n tvidameteShAM balaM bhImAbhirakShitam .. 1-10 ..

sanskrit: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः । भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥ १-११ ॥
translation: Therefore, all ye standing in your respective divisions (places) in the different ranks should chiefly guard Bhishma.
itrans: ayaneShu cha sarveShu yathAbhAgamavasthitAH . bhIShmamevAbhirakShantu bhavantaH sarva eva hi .. 1-11 ..

sanskrit: तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥ १-१२ ॥
translation: In order to cheer him, the aged Kuru, the grandsire (Bhishma) the glorious, made a lion's roar and blew his conch.
itrans: tasya sa~njanayanharSha.n kuruvR^iddhaH pitAmahaH . si.nhanAda.n vinadyochchaiH sha~Nkha.n dadhmau pratApavAn .. 1-12 ..

sanskrit: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥ १-१३ ॥
translation: At the same time were sounded the conches, wardrums tabors, and drums, horns, and the sound became tumultuous.
itrans: tataH sha~NkhAshcha bheryashcha paNavAnakagomukhAH . sahasaivAbhyahanyanta sa shabdastumulo.abhavat .. 1-13 ..

sanskrit: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥ १-१४ ॥
translation: Then seated in their great chariot yoked to white horses, Madhava and the Pandaya (Arjuna) blew their divine conches.
itrans: tataH shvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau . mAdhavaH pANDavashchaiva divyau sha~Nkhau pradadhmatuH .. 1-14 ..

sanskrit: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १-१५ ॥
translation: Hrishikesa (the ruler of the senses) blew his Panchajanya and Dhananjaya his Devadatta; Vrikodara (Bhima) of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch Poundra.
itrans: pA~nchajanya.n hR^iShIkesho devadatta.n dhana~njayaH . pauNDra.n dadhmau mahAsha~NkhaM bhImakarmA vR^ikodaraH .. 1-15 ..

sanskrit: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १-१६ ॥
translation: The King Yudhishtira, the son of Kunti (blew his conch) Anantavijaya; and Nakula and Sahadeva, (their conches), Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
itrans: anantavijaya.n rAjA kuntIputro yudhiShThiraH . nakulaH sahadevashcha sughoShamaNipuShpakau .. 1-16 ..

sanskrit: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १-१७ ॥
translation: And Kâsya of the great bow, Sikhandi of the great chariot and Satyaki the unconquered,
itrans: kAshyashcha parameShvAsaH shikhaNDI cha mahArathaH . dhR^iShTadyumno virATashcha sAtyakishchAparAjitaH .. 1-17 ..

sanskrit: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥ १-१८ ॥
translation: Drupada, and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of earth, Saubhadra the mighty-armed, all separately blew their conches.
itrans: drupado draupadeyAshcha sarvashaH pR^ithivIpate . saubhadrashcha mahAbAhuH sha~NkhAndadhmuH pR^ithakpR^ithak .. 1-18 ..

sanskrit: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलोऽभ्यनुनादयन् ॥ १-१९ ॥
translation: That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, resounding through earth and sky.
itrans: sa ghoSho dhArtarAShTrANAM hR^idayAni vyadArayat . nabhashcha pR^ithivI.n chaiva tumulo.abhyanunAdayan .. 1-19 ..

sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ १-२० ॥
translation: Then having seen the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order, the throwing of missiles, having almost commenced, Arjuna the son of Pandu whose emblem is an ape took up his bow.
itrans: atha vyavasthitAndR^iShTvA dhArtarAShTrAn kapidhvajaH . pravR^itte shastrasampAte dhanurudyamya pANDavaH .. 1-20 ..

sanskrit: हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।        अर्जुन उवाच । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ १-२१ ॥
translation: And then speaketh (spoke) this word to Hrishikesa, O Lord of earth, Achyuta, stay my chariot in the middle of these two armies,
itrans: hR^iShIkesha.n tadA vAkyamidamAha mahIpate .        arjuna uvAcha . senayorubhayormadhye ratha.n sthApaya me.achyuta .. 1-21 ..

sanskrit: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान् । कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे ॥ १-२२ ॥
translation: So that I may see who have stood up eager for battle and with whom I should fight in this outbreaking war;
itrans: yAvadetAnnirIkShe.ahaM yoddhukAmAnavasthitAn . kairmayA saha yoddhavyamasmin raNasamudyame .. 1-22 ..

sanskrit: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥ १-२३ ॥
translation: So that I may also note those who have here gathered together and intend to gratify the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
itrans: yotsyamAnAnavekShe.ahaM ya ete.atra samAgatAH . dhArtarAShTrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyachikIrShavaH .. 1-23 ..

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥ १-२४ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: -Thus spoken to by Gudakesa (one that has overcome sleep), O Bharata, Hrishikesa drove the best of chariots to the middle of the two armies;
itrans: sa~njaya uvAcha . evamukto hR^iShIkesho guDAkeshena bhArata . senayorubhayormadhye sthApayitvA rathottamam .. 1-24 ..

sanskrit: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥ १-२५ ॥
translation: And having stayed it in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the princes of earth, said, Partha, behold all these Kuras.
itrans: bhIShmadroNapramukhataH sarveShA.n cha mahIkShitAm . uvAcha pArtha pashyaitAnsamavetAnkurUniti .. 1-25 ..

sanskrit: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् । आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥ १-२६ ॥
itrans: tatrApashyatsthitAnpArthaH pitR^Inatha pitAmahAn . AchAryAnmAtulAnbhrAtR^InputrAnpautrAnsakhI.nstathA .. 1-26 ..

sanskrit: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥ १-२७ ॥
translation: There standing up in both the armies, Partha saw fathers (uncles) and grandfathers, teachers and mother's brothers, brothers (cousins), sons and grandsons, comrades, fathers-in-law, and benefactors; seeing all these kinsmen standing arrayed, that Kunti's son was deeply moved to pity and in sadness spoke this (as follows).
itrans: shvashurAnsuhR^idashchaiva senayorubhayorapi . tAnsamIkShya sa kaunteyaH sarvAnbandhUnavasthitAn .. 1-27 ..

sanskrit: कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् ।        अर्जुन उवाच । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥ १-२८ ॥
translation: “At seeing these my kinsmen, O Krishna, that stand up eager to fight, my limbs fail, and my mouth is parched, my body quivers and my hair stands on end;
itrans: kR^ipayA parayAviShTo viShIdannidamabravIt .        arjuna uvAcha . dR^iShTvema.n svajana.n kR^iShNa yuyutsu.n samupasthitam .. 1-28 ..

sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ १-२९ ॥
itrans: sIdanti mama gAtrANi mukha.n cha parishuShyati . vepathushcha sharIre me romaharShashcha jAyate .. 1-29 ..

sanskrit: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥ १-३० ॥
translation: Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin burns all over. And I am not able to stand, and my mind is whirling, and I see evil omens, 0 Kesava,
itrans: gANDIva.n sra.nsate hastAttvakchaiva paridahyate . na cha shaknomyavasthAtuM bhramatIva cha me manaH .. 1-30 ..

sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥ १-३१ ॥
itrans: nimittAni cha pashyAmi viparItAni keshava . na cha shreyo.anupashyAmi hatvA svajanamAhave .. 1-31 ..

sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥ १-३२ ॥
itrans: na kA~NkShe vijaya.n kR^iShNa na cha rAjya.n sukhAni cha . ki.n no rAjyena govinda kiM bhogairjIvitena vA .. 1-32 ..

sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥ १-३३ ॥
itrans: yeShAmarthe kA~NkShita.n no rAjyaM bhogAH sukhAni cha . ta ime.avasthitA yuddhe prANA.nstyaktvA dhanAni cha .. 1-33 ..

sanskrit: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ १-३४ ॥
itrans: AchAryAH pitaraH putrAstathaiva cha pitAmahAH . mAtulAH shvashurAH pautrAH shyAlAH sambandhinastathA .. 1-34 ..

sanskrit: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥ १-३५ ॥
translation: Nor do I see anything good in slaying my kinsmen in battle; Krishna, I wish not for victory, nor kingdom nor pleasures; what is kingdom to us, o Govinda, what enjoyments or even life? Those for whose sake kingdom is desired as well as pleasures and their means - all those stand here in battle abandoning life and riches, the preceptors, fathers (uncles), sons, as well as grandfathers, mother's brothers, fathers-in-law, grandsons brothers-in-law and (other) kith and kin; I do not wish; to slay these, O Madhusudana, though they (would) kill (me), and though it be for the kingship of the three worlds; how then for earth? In slaying the sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure can be ours, Janardana?
itrans: etAnna hantumichChAmi ghnato.api madhusUdana . api trailokyarAjyasya hetoH kiM nu mahIkR^ite .. 1-35 ..

sanskrit: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥ १-३६ ॥
itrans: nihatya dhArtarAShTrAnnaH kA prItiH syAjjanArdana . pApamevAshrayedasmAnhatvaitAnAtatAyinaH .. 1-36 ..

sanskrit: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥ १-३७ ॥
itrans: tasmAnnArhA vaya.n hantuM dhArtarAShTrAnsvabAndhavAn . svajana.n hi katha.n hatvA sukhinaH syAma mAdhava .. 1-37 ..

sanskrit: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥ १-३८ ॥
itrans: yadyapyete na pashyanti lobhopahatachetasaH . kulakShayakR^ita.n doShaM mitradrohe cha pAtakam .. 1-38 ..

sanskrit: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥ १-३९ ॥
translation: Only sin will take hold of us in slaying these, for though they are ruffians, we kill our own kinsmen. So, it is not fit that we kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our kinsmen. Indeed, how can we be happy, O Madhava, having killed our kith and kin? However, those infatuated with greed do not see the guilt) in the destruction of the race and do not see the sin in being treacherous (to the lives of) friends. Why should not we also) see that it is wise) to turn away from such a sin, O Janardana, we who clearly perceive the evils in the destruction of races?
itrans: katha.n na j~neyamasmAbhiH pApAdasmAnnivartitum . kulakShayakR^ita.n doShaM prapashyadbhirjanArdana .. 1-39 ..

sanskrit: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥ १-४० ॥
itrans: kulakShaye praNashyanti kuladharmAH sanAtanAH . dharme naShTe kula.n kR^itsnamadharmo.abhibhavatyuta .. 1-40 ..

sanskrit: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥ १-४१ ॥
itrans: adharmAbhibhavAtkR^iShNa praduShyanti kulastriyaH . strIShu duShTAsu vArShNeya jAyate varNasa~NkaraH .. 1-41 ..

sanskrit: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ १-४२ ॥
itrans: sa~Nkaro narakAyaiva kulaghnAnAM kulasya cha . patanti pitaro hyeShAM luptapiNDodakakriyAH .. 1-42 ..

sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥ १-४३ ॥
itrans: doShairetaiH kulaghnAnAM varNasa~NkarakArakaiH . utsAdyante jAtidharmAH kuladharmAshcha shAshvatAH .. 1-43 ..

sanskrit: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥ १-४४॥
translation: (What are the evils?) In the destruction of the race, the virtues of the race handed down from time immemorial perish altogether. When virtue is lost, vice invades the race. Being overpowered with vice the women of the race become corrupt; women corrupted, O Varshneya, 'the confusion of the Varnas (castes) arises; (such) confusion of castes leads to heil the race as well as those who prove its ruin; for their ancestors fall deprived of rice-balls and libations of water. By these misdeeds of the slayers of family leading to the confusion of castes, the eternal caste virtues of the race are destroyed, 0 Janardana, and men who have lost the virtues of the family, we are told, surely live forever in hell.
itrans: utsannakuladharmANAM manuShyANA.n janArdana . narake niyata.n vAso bhavatItyanushushruma .. 1-44..

sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥ १-४५ ॥
itrans: aho bata mahatpApa.n kartuM vyavasitA vayam . yadrAjyasukhalobhena hantuM svajanamudyatAH .. 1-45 ..

sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥ १-४६ ॥
translation: Alas! to commit a great sin we have made up our mind, in that we, desirous of the kingdom and pleasures thereof, are prepared to slay our kinsmen; (so I think) it would be much better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra with weapons in their hands should in the battlefield slay me unarmed and unresisting.
itrans: yadi mAmapratIkAramashastra.n shastrapANayaH . dhArtarAShTrA raNe hanyustanme kShemataraM bhavet .. 1-46 ..

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥ १-४७ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: “Having thus spoken on the battlefield Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow, his mind perplexed with grief.”
itrans: sa~njaya uvAcha . evamuktvArjunaH sa~Nkhye rathopastha upAvishat . visR^ijya sashara.n chApa.n shokasa.nvignamAnasaH .. 1-47 ..

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ २-१ ॥
translation: Sanjaya said :-To him (Arjuna), thus overcome with pity, with eyes dimmed with tears and grown despondent, Madhusudana spoke these words.
itrans: sa~njaya uvAcha . ta.n tathA kR^ipayAviShTamashrupUrNAkulekShaNam . viShIdantamida.n vAkyamuvAcha madhusUdanaH .. 2-1 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥ २-२ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said :-Whence has this infatuation thus inopportunely invaded thee, which behoves the ignoble and stands in the way of Svarga and glory, O Arjuna ?
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . kutastvA kashmalamida.n viShame samupasthitam . anAryajuShTamasvargyamakIrtikaramarjuna .. 2-2 ..

sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥ २-३ ॥
translation: To despondency do not give thyself up, O Partha ; it does not become in thee. Shake off the paltry faint-heartedness; and stand up, O slayer of enemies.
itrans: klaibyaM mA sma gamaH pArtha naitattvayyupapadyate . kShudra.n hR^idayadaurbalya.n tyaktvottiShTha parantapa .. 2-3 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥ २-४ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Madhusudana, how in battle shall I attack the venerable Bhishma and Drona with arrows, O slayer of foes?
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . kathaM bhIShmamaha.n sa~Nkhye droNa.n cha madhusUdana . iShubhiH pratiyotsyAmi pUjArhAvarisUdana .. 2-4 ..

sanskrit: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्        श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके । हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव        भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ २-५ ॥
translation: Better to live by begging in this world than to slay the glorious elders, who are pursuing (great) purposes. On the other hand, if I slay the venerable elders, I should enjoy the pleasures besprinkled with their blood.
itrans: gurUnahatvA hi mahAnubhAvAn.h        shreyo bhoktuM bhaikShyamapIha loke . hatvArthakAmA.nstu gurUnihaiva        bhu~njIya bhogAn rudhirapradigdhAn .. 2-5 ..

sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो        यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्-        तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ २-६ ॥
translation: Nor do we know which is more probable, that we conquer them or that they conquer us; those very sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, whom having slain we might not wish to live.
itrans: na chaitadvidmaH kataranno garIyo        yadvA jayema yadi vA no jayeyuH . yAneva hatvA na jijIviShAmas-        te.avasthitAH pramukhe dhArtarAShTrAH .. 2-6 ..

sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः        पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे        शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥ २-७ ॥
translation: My very nature, natural courage, is overpowered with the vice of faint-heartedness. I am bewildered as to what is right and ask Thee Which is surely the preferable course? Please tell me decisively, I am Thy disciple, rule me who am seeking Thy refuge.
itrans: kArpaNyadoShopahatasvabhAvaH        pR^ichChAmi tvAM dharmasammUDhachetAH . yachChreyaH syAnnishchitaM brUhi tanme        shiShyaste.aha.n shAdhi mA.n tvAM prapannam .. 2-7 ..

sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्        यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं        राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥ २-८ ॥
translation: Indeed, I see not what could drive away the grief that withers my senses, even if I should on earth obtain the richest kingdom without any rivals, or even the lordship over the gods.
itrans: na hi prapashyAmi mamApanudyAd.h        yachChokamuchChoShaNamindriyANAm . avApya bhUmAvasapatnamR^iddha.n        rAjya.n surANAmapi chAdhipatyam .. 2-8 ..

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥ २-९ ॥
itrans: sa~njaya uvAcha . evamuktvA hR^iShIkesha.n guDAkeshaH parantapa . na yotsya iti govindamuktvA tUShNIM babhUva ha .. 2-9 ..

sanskrit: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥ २-१० ॥
translation: Sanjaya said: - Having thus spoken to Hrishikesa, Gudakesa, the terror of foes, said to Govinda "I will not fight, and became silent. 0 Bharata, Hrishikesa in a laughing mood spoke these words to him that (stood) despondent in the midst of the two armies.
itrans: tamuvAcha hR^iShIkeshaH prahasanniva bhArata . senayorubhayormadhye viShIdantamida.n vachaH .. 2-10 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥ २-११ ॥
translation: With the knowledge of the greatness of the Lord and devotion to Him, whatever is done as His worship or as one's own duty, becomes highly righteous; and the highest virtue to be practised by the Kshatriyas is the chastisement of the haters of Narayana and their followers. To Arjuna who out of love for his kinsmen regards that duty as something unrighteous, Sri Krishna intends in the whole of the Gita Sâstra to show clearly that his highest duty is of the aforesaid description and everything in contravention of it becomes violation of duty. Now to begin with the Lord points out that his grief proceeds from lack of judgement. The blessed Lord said: - Thou hast grieved for those that should not be grieved for and yet speakest words of wisdom; the wise grieve not for the dead and (as) for the living.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . ashochyAnanvashochastvaM praj~nAvAdA.nshcha bhAShase . gatAsUnagatAsU.nshcha nAnushochanti paNDitAH .. 2-11 ..

sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ २-१२ ॥
translation: Words of wisdom, i.e., arguments framed with thy own understanding, not agreeable to the wise. The term Pragna-Vada may also mean words or arguments contrary to the views of the wise (Pragna+avada). For in the words of Arjuna Seeing my kinsmen &c (दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्णे), there is no word or argument acceptable to the wise. And the wise never speak of the chastisement of the haters of Narayana and their followers as Adharma (unrighteous). The hemistich explains why those about to perish need not be grieved for. For the dead shall be taken in the sense of ‘for those whom death awaits’. And for the living, in the sense of ‘as for the living': i.e., the wise do not grieve for those who are about to perish just as they would not grieve for the living; or just as the living do not deserve to be grieved for, so also those whom death is about to overtake as well as the dead need not be grieved for. The copulative conjunction has the force of 'like' or 'as implying comparison. Hence the qualification in the first half ‘those that should not be grieved for’. Then arises the question 'why the wise do not grieve, how A's arguments are not acceptable to them. The matter should be analysed thus: whether A's grief is on account of the destruction of their souls, or it is on account of the destruction of their body or whether it is on account of the belief that the body being dissolved the soul ceases to be, and the destruction of the one is the destruction of the other. To refute the first of these three positions, He says: Nor at any time verily I was not, nor thou, nor these princes of men; nor verily shall we all ever cease to be hereafter.
itrans: na tvevAha.n jAtu nAsa.n na tva.n neme janAdhipAH . na chaiva na bhaviShyAmaH sarve vayamataH param .. 2-12 ..

sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ २-१३ ॥
translation: Just as childhood, youth (and) old age (befall) the dweller of the body while in the same body, so also change of body befalls (him); the wise one therefore does not become perplexed there at.
itrans: dehino.asminyathA dehe kaumAra.n yauvana.n jarA . tathA dehAntaraprAptirdhIrastatra na muhyati .. 2-13 ..

sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः । आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ २-१४ ॥
translation: The contacts, indeed, of the objects, O Kunti's son, (do they alone) become the cause of hot and cold (sensations), pleasure and pain? They come and go, they are impermanent; O Bharata, render them ineffectual.
itrans: mAtrAsparshAstu kaunteya shItoShNasukhaduHkhadAH . AgamApAyino.anityAstA.nstitikShasva bhArata .. 2-14 ..

sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ २-१५ ॥
translation: O Bull among men, whomsoever these contacts indeed do not agitate, that Purusha, who unperturbed regards equally pleasure and pain, becomes fit for immortality.
itrans: ya.n hi na vyathayantyete puruShaM puruSharShabha . samaduHkhasukha.n dhIra.n so.amR^itatvAya kalpate .. 2-15 ..

sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ २-१६ ॥
translation: (a) From unrighteousness results no happiness (good), (just as) from righteousness results nothing miserable (bad); of both these (facts) the conclusion (truth) as handed down is actually observed by those who have seen the Truth.
itrans: nAsato vidyate bhAvo nAbhAvo vidyate sataH . ubhayorapi dR^iShTo.antastvanayostattvadarshibhiH .. 2-16 ..

sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ २-१७ ॥
translation: Absolutely indestructible is that by itself, know thou, by which all this is pervaded; no one can work the destruction of this which is irreducible
itrans: avinAshi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamida.n tatam . vinAshamavyayasyAsya na kashchitkartumarhati .. 2-17 ..

sanskrit: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः । अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ २-१८ ॥
translation: Destructible are these bodies of the eternal (souls) who are dwellers in body, who are indestructible and (like unto the) immeasurable; therefore, do thou fight, Bharata.
itrans: antavanta ime dehA nityasyoktAH sharIriNaH . anAshino.aprameyasya tasmAdyudhyasva bhArata .. 2-18 ..

sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् । उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ २-१९ ॥
translation: He who thinks this (person) to be the slayer and he who thinks this (person) to be slain-those two do not perceive (the truth); (for) this (person) does not slay; nor is he slain
itrans: ya ena.n vetti hantAra.n yashchainaM manyate hatam . ubhau tau na vijAnIto nAya.n hanti na hanyate .. 2-19 ..

sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्        नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो        न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २-२० ॥
translation: Neither is he born nor doth he dies; and having been once in existence, he is not to be produced again; he is unborn and indestructible, is eternally of the same character; he is a wanderer through bodies; he is not slain, when the body is slain.
itrans: na jAyate mriyate vA kadAchin.h        nAyaM bhUtvA bhavitA vA na bhUyaH . ajo nityaH shAshvato.ayaM purANo        na hanyate hanyamAne sharIre .. 2-20 ..

sanskrit: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् । कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥ २-२१ ॥
translation: He who knows this (person) to be incapable of being lost or destroyed, to be unborn and unmodified, --how can he, such a person, think of himself as killing or causing another to kill or to be killed.
itrans: vedAvinAshina.n nitya.n ya enamajamavyayam . katha.n sa puruShaH pArtha ka.n ghAtayati hanti kam .. 2-21 ..

sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय        नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा-        न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥ २-२२ ॥
translation: Just as a person having cast off the worn-out clothes gets other and fresh ones, so also the dweller of the body casts off the worn out bodies and goes on to other and fresh ones.
itrans: vAsA.nsi jIrNAni yathA vihAya        navAni gR^ihNAti naro.aparANi . tathA sharIrANi vihAya jIrNA-        nyanyAni sa.nyAti navAni dehI .. 2-22 ..

sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ २-२३ ॥
translation: Weapons do not cut him, fire does not burn him, waters do not wet him, wind does not dry him (-him who is the dweller in the body).
itrans: naina.n Chindanti shastrANi naina.n dahati pAvakaH . na chaina.n kledayantyApo na shoShayati mArutaH .. 2-23 ..

sanskrit: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २-२४ ॥
translation: He is uncleavable, he is incombustible, (he) can neither be wetted nor dried at all; he is eternal, all pervading, stable, unmoved, and (connected) with the sound.
itrans: achChedyo.ayamadAhyo.ayamakledyo.ashoShya eva cha . nityaH sarvagataH sthANurachalo.aya.n sanAtanaH .. 2-24 ..

sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते । तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२५ ॥
translation: He is unmanifest; He is incomprehensible; He is not changeable; He is (so) described (by the Srutis). Therefore, it is not fit that having known this (soul) to be such, thou shouldst grieve.
itrans: avyakto.ayamachintyo.ayamavikAryo.ayamuchyate . tasmAdeva.n viditvaina.n nAnushochitumarhasi .. 2-25 ..

sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२६ ॥
translation: Or if thou thinkest of him as ever born or as ever dead, even then, O mighty armed, it is not fit that thou grievest.
itrans: atha chaina.n nityajAta.n nitya.n vA manyase mR^itam . tathApi tvaM mahAbAho naiva.n shochitumarhasi .. 2-26 ..

sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-२७ ॥
translation: For, certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore, in matters inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.
itrans: jAtasya hi dhruvo mR^ityurdhruva.n janma mR^itasya cha . tasmAdaparihArye.arthe na tva.n shochitumarhasi .. 2-27 ..

sanskrit: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ २-२८ ॥
translation: Bodies (of beings) have their origin in the Unmanifest, have a manifest middle (state) and indeed have their end, O Bharata, in the Unmanifest; What is there to be grieved at?
itrans: avyaktAdIni bhUtAni vyaktamadhyAni bhArata . avyaktanidhanAnyeva tatra kA paridevanA .. 2-28 ..

sanskrit: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन-        माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः । आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति        श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥ २-२९ ॥
translation: Someone perceives Him as a wonder; likewise, someone speaks of Him as a wonder; and some one hears of Him as a wonder; yet having heard, one may not know Him at all.
itrans: Ashcharyavatpashyati kashchidena-        mAshcharyavadvadati tathaiva chAnyaH . AshcharyavachchainamanyaH shR^iNoti        shrutvApyena.n veda na chaiva kashchit .. 2-29 ..

sanskrit: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २-३० ॥
translation: The dweller in the body, is ever indestructible; (for) He is, Bharata in the body of everyone; therefore, thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.
itrans: dehI nityamavadhyo.aya.n dehe sarvasya bhArata . tasmAtsarvANi bhUtAni na tva.n shochitumarhasi .. 2-30 ..

sanskrit: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि । धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥ २-३१ ॥
translation: Even having regard to thine own duty thou shouldest not tremble, for a Kshatriya has nothing to do more praiseworthy than (to wage) the dutiful war.
itrans: svadharmamapi chAvekShya na vikampitumarhasi . dharmyAddhi yuddhAchChreyo.anyatkShatriyasya na vidyate .. 2-31 ..

sanskrit: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् । सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥ २-३२ ॥
translation: And by chance (Fortune) has sought (thee); the gates of Heaven are thrown open. Only the happy Kshatriyas, O Partha, come upon such a war,
itrans: yadR^ichChayA chopapanna.n svargadvAramapAvR^itam . sukhinaH kShatriyAH pArtha labhante yuddhamIdR^isham .. 2-32 ..

sanskrit: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं सङ्ग्रामं न करिष्यसि । ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-३३ ॥
translation: Further, if thou will not wage this righteous war, thou wilt be abandoning (losing) thine own duty (character) and honour and thereby thou shalt incur -sin.
itrans: atha chettvamimaM dharmya.n sa~NgrAma.n na kariShyasi . tataH svadharma.n kIrti.n cha hitvA pApamavApsyasi .. 2-33 ..

sanskrit: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् । सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥ २-३४ ॥
translation: Besides, all beings (men) will recount thy everlasting dishonour ; and to one who is highly esteemed, dishonour exceedeth death...
itrans: akIrti.n chApi bhUtAni kathayiShyanti te.avyayAm . sambhAvitasya chAkIrtirmaraNAdatirichyate .. 2-34 ..

sanskrit: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः । येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ २-३५ ॥
translation: The Maharathas (great warriors will think thee as having withdrawn thyself from the battle only through fear, and amongst those warriors by whom thou hast been esteemed, thou wilt come to be slighted.
itrans: bhayAdraNAduparataM ma.nsyante tvAM mahArathAH . yeShA.n cha tvaM bahumato bhUtvA yAsyasi lAghavam .. 2-35 ..

sanskrit: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः । निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥ २-३६ ॥
translation: Thine enemies will utter many a reproach unworthy to be spoken, slandering thy prowess and ability; than which what could possibly be greater misery?
itrans: avAchyavAdA.nshcha bahUnvadiShyanti tavAhitAH . nindantastava sAmarthyaM tato duHkhatara.n nu kim .. 2-36 ..

sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् । तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ २-३७ ॥
translation: If slain, thou shalt obtain Svarga; or if victorious, thou shalt enjoy the earth; therefore, stand up, Kunti's son, determined upon fighting
itrans: hato vA prApsyasi svarga.n jitvA vA bhokShyase mahIm . tasmAduttiShTha kaunteya yuddhAya kR^itanishchayaH .. 2-37 ..

sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-३८ ॥
translation: Considering as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, prepare thyself for battle; thereby thou shalt not at all incur sin.
itrans: sukhaduHkhe same kR^itvA lAbhAlAbhau jayAjayau . tato yuddhAya yujyasva naivaM pApamavApsyasi .. 2-38 ..

sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु । बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ २-३९ ॥
translation: This knowledge in respect of Sankhya has been imparted to thee; and in respect of Yoga, too, listen to this (what follows), imbued with which knowledge, O Partha, thou shalt cast away the bonds of Karma.
itrans: eShA te.abhihitA sA~Nkhye buddhiryoge tvimA.n shR^iNu . bud.hdhyA yukto yayA pArtha karmabandhaM prahAsyasi .. 2-39 ..

sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥ २-४० ॥
translation: Moreover, there is no loss here of endeavours; there arises no evil; even a little of this duty saves (man) from the great fear.
itrans: nehAbhikramanAsho.asti pratyavAyo na vidyate . svalpamapyasya dharmasya trAyate mahato bhayAt .. 2-40 ..

sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ २-४१ ॥
translation: The teaching which forms the true conclusion is here but one, O delight of the Kurus; (whereas) the teachings of those who have not come to.be true conclusion are many-branched and endless.
itrans: vyavasAyAtmikA buddhirekeha kurunandana . bahushAkhA hyanantAshcha buddhayo.avyavasAyinAm .. 2-41 ..

sanskrit: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ २-४२ ॥
itrans: yAmimAM puShpitAM vAchaM pravadantyavipashchitaH . vedavAdaratAH pArtha nAnyadastIti vAdinaH .. 2-42 ..

sanskrit: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् । क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ २-४३ ॥
translation: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्‍तानां तयाऽपहृतचेतसाम् ।
itrans: kAmAtmAnaH svargaparA janmakarmaphalapradAm . kriyAvisheShabahulAM bhogaishvaryagatiM prati .. 2-43 ..

sanskrit: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ २-४४ ॥
translation: Those who from want of insight, rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, saying:
itrans: bhogaishvaryaprasaktAnA.n tayApahR^itachetasAm . vyavasAyAtmikA buddhiH samAdhau na vidhIyate .. 2-44 ..

sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ २-४५ ॥
translation: The Vedas seem to speak of what pertains to the three qualities; get thyself, O Arjuna, free from the effect of the three qualities; stand aloof from the pairs of opposites; always take thy stand on the Eternally Excellent; be free from the cares of gain and security :(and) ever have the Lord with thee.
itrans: traiguNyaviShayA vedA nistraiguNyo bhavArjuna . nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakShema AtmavAn .. 2-45 ..

sanskrit: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके । तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ २-४६ ॥
translation: What purpose is realised in a wide expanse of water on all sides, that purpose (to' that extent) is (realised) in a well; (in the same manner), what purpose is realised through all the Vedas, that purpose to that extent is realised by the learned man, who sees Brahman.
itrans: yAvAnartha udapAne sarvataH samplutodake . tAvAnsarveShu vedeShu brAhmaNasya vijAnataH .. 2-46 ..

sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ २-४७ ॥
translation: Only in respect of action there is eligibility in thee, never in respect of its fruits; (so) do not make the fruit' a motive for thy action, nor lot there be on thy part any attachment to inaction.
itrans: karmaNyevAdhikAraste mA phaleShu kadAchana . mA karmaphalaheturbhUrmA te sa~Ngo.astvakarmaNi .. 2-47 ..

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ २-४८ ॥
translation: Taking thy stand on Yoga do the duties, O Dhananjaya, renouncing attachment, being alike in success and failure; (this) state of being alike is called Yoga.
itrans: yogasthaH kuru karmANi sa~Nga.n tyaktvA dhana~njaya . sid.hdhyasid.hdhyoH samo bhUtvA samatva.n yoga uchyate .. 2-48 ..

sanskrit: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ २-४९ ॥
translation: Far, far inferior, indeed is Karwa ta knowledge as a means, O Dhananjaya; take thou refuge in knowledge; pitiable are they who have a motive for their action.
itrans: dUreNa hyavara.n karma buddhiyogAddhana~njaya . buddhau sharaNamanvichCha kR^ipaNAH phalahetavaH .. 2-49 ..

sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ २-५० ॥
translation: With knowledge (of God) he casts off here both good and evil (deeds); therefore, exert thyself for the Yoga (means of knowledge); (for) the Yoga is the most efficacious in the midst of duties.
itrans: buddhiyukto jahAtIha ubhe sukR^itaduShkR^ite . tasmAdyogAya yujyasva yogaH karmasu kaushalam .. 2-50 ..

sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः । जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ २-५१ ॥
translation: Those who gain knowledge (by) renouncing the fruit of Karma, surely become wise and released from the bonds of birth, and attain to the goal beyond misery.
itrans: karmajaM buddhiyuktA hi phalaM tyaktvA manIShiNaH . janmabandhavinirmuktAH padaM gachChantyanAmayam .. 2-51 ..

sanskrit: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ २-५२ ॥
translation: When thy mind shall get over the evil of misapprehension, then shalt thou attain to the full benefit of what has been heard and should be heard.
itrans: yadA te mohakalilaM buddhirvyatitariShyati . tadA gantAsi nirvedaM shrotavyasya shrutasya cha .. 2-52 ..

sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २-५३ ॥
translation: When thy reason at conflict with Srutis shall stand unshaken (and) when in deep meditation it shall be. unperturbed, then shalt thou attain unto Yoga.
itrans: shrutivipratipannA te yadA sthAsyati nishchalA . samAdhAvachalA buddhistadA yogamavApsyasi .. 2-53 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव । स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥ २-५४ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Of him whose wisdom is mature and who is in meditation, what is the description, O Kesava? He whose perception has become steadfast, what should he talk about, what should he sit at, what should he go to?
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . sthitapraj~nasya kA bhAShA samAdhisthasya keshava . sthitadhIH kiM prabhASheta kimAsIta vrajeta kim .. 2-54 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ २-५५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: - When a man eschews, O Partha, all the desires in the heart, and, being confirmed in the Lord, finds satisfaction by the Lord, then is he called one of steady wisdom.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . prajahAti yadA kAmAnsarvAnpArtha manogatAn . AtmanyevAtmanA tuShTaH sthitapraj~nastadochyate .. 2-55 ..

sanskrit: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः । वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ २-५६ ॥
translation: He whose mind is unagitated amid pains, who is destitute of longing for pleasures, of passion and fear and anger,-- he is called a sage of steadfast wisdom.
itrans: duHkheShvanudvignamanAH sukheShu vigataspR^ihaH . vItarAgabhayakrodhaH sthitadhIrmuniruchyate .. 2-56 ..

sanskrit: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-५७ ॥
translation: He who is on every side without 'Strong attachments, neither rejoices at nor abhors whatever happens, auspicious or inauspicious, (good or bad), of such a one wisdom becomes established (steadfast).
itrans: yaH sarvatrAnabhisnehastattatprApya shubhAshubham . nAbhinandati na dveShTi tasya praj~nA pratiShThitA .. 2-57 ..

sanskrit: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-५८ ॥
translation: Further, when again, - he can, without effort, even as a tortoise, does its limbs, withdraw all his senses from their objects, his wisdom is securely established.
itrans: yadA sa.nharate chAyaM kUrmo.a~NgAnIva sarvashaH . indriyANIndriyArthebhyastasya praj~nA pratiShThitA .. 2-58 ..

sanskrit: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ २-५९ ॥
translation: The objects of sense, not the longing for them, turn away from the person who abstains from food; even that longing in him clears off, having seen the Supreme.
itrans: viShayA vinivartante nirAhArasya dehinaH . rasavarja.n raso.apyasya para.n dR^iShTvA nivartate .. 2-59 ..

sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ २-६० ॥
translation: Exert though he may, O Kunti's son, be he the learned, the turbulent senses of the person, indeed, carry his mind away.
itrans: yatato hyapi kaunteya puruShasya vipashchitaH . indriyANi pramAthIni haranti prasabhaM manaH .. 2-60 ..

sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-६१ ॥
translation: Having restrained them all, he should sit in contemplation that I only am his Supreme Lord ; wisdom becomes firmly established of him who has surely the senses under his control.
itrans: tAni sarvANi sa.nyamya yukta AsIta matparaH . vashe hi yasyendriyANi tasya praj~nA pratiShThitA .. 2-61 ..

sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ २-६२ ॥
translation: In him who muses of the objects of sense an attachment to them is formed; from the attachment arises desire; from desire arises anger;
itrans: dhyAyato viShayAnpu.nsaH sa~NgasteShUpajAyate . sa~NgAtsa~njAyate kAmaH kAmAtkrodho.abhijAyate .. 2-62 ..

sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ २-६३ ॥
translation: From anger results the wrong wish; from (this) wrong wish, forgetfulness (of Law); from (this) forgetfulness, loss of judgement; from the loss of judgement, he perishes.
itrans: krodhAdbhavati sammohaH sammohAtsmR^itivibhramaH . smR^itibhra.nshAd buddhinAsho buddhinAshAtpraNashyati .. 2-63 ..

sanskrit: रागद्वेषविमुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् । orवियुक्तैस्तुआत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ २-६४ ॥
translation: But be who with the senses free of Like and Dislike and obedient to self (him) experiences their objects, finds an obedient mind and attains serenity (of mind).
itrans: rAgadveShavimuktaistu viShayAnindriyaishcharan . ##or##viyuktaistuAtmavashyairvidheyAtmA prasAdamadhigachChati .. 2-64 ..

sanskrit: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ २-६५ ॥
translation: Serenity rising, the extinction of all his miseries comes about; for, the perception of him who is of it serene mind soon becomes steadied.
itrans: prasAde sarvaduHkhAnA.n hAnirasyopajAyate . prasannachetaso hyAshu buddhiH paryavatiShThate .. 2-65 ..

sanskrit: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ २-६६ ॥
translation: Contemplation is not possible for him who does not restrain the mind.; for him who does not contemplate, direct perception does not arise, for him who has not gained the perception, release is impossible. Without release, whence is happiness?
itrans: nAsti buddhirayuktasya na chAyuktasya bhAvanA . na chAbhAvayataH shAntirashAntasya kutaH sukham .. 2-66 ..

sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ २-६७ ॥
translation: That the mind is made to follow the wandering senses sends his understanding adrift, even as the wind does the vessel upon the waters.
itrans: indriyANAM hi charatAM yanmano.anuvidhIyate . tadasya harati praj~nAM vAyurnAvamivAmbhasi .. 2-67 ..

sanskrit: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ २-६८ ॥
translation: Therefore, o Mighty armed, of whom the senses are all withdrawn from their objects, of him wisdom becomes steadfast.
itrans: tasmAdyasya mahAbAho nigR^ihItAni sarvashaH . indriyANIndriyArthebhyastasya praj~nA pratiShThitA .. 2-68 ..

sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ २-६९ ॥
translation: In respect of that which is the night of all beings the man of self-restraint keeps awake; in respect of which the brings are awake, that is the night of the contemplating sage who sees (the Lord).
itrans: yA nishA sarvabhUtAnAM tasyA.n jAgarti sa.nyamI . yasyA.n jAgrati bhUtAni sA nishA pashyato muneH .. 2-69 ..

sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं        समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे        स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ २-७० ॥
translation: He attains to heaven, into whom all desires flow even as waters (rivers) flow into the ocean which is being constantly filled but remains in the same unchanged condition, not he who desires pleasure (the objects of sense).
itrans: ApUryamANamachalapratiShTha.n        samudramApaH pravishanti yadvat . tadvatkAmA yaM pravishanti sarve        sa shAntimApnoti na kAmakAmI .. 2-70 ..

sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ २-७१ ॥
translation: He who, loosed from all the (prohibited) wishes, from the . fancy of being the (absolute) master and the (absolute) agent, experiences all the objects of desire) without any attachment,-- he is the man, he attains to perfect bliss.
itrans: vihAya kAmAnyaH sarvAnpumA.nshcharati niHspR^ihaH . nirmamo niraha~NkAraH sa shAntimadhigachChati .. 2-71 ..

sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ २-७२ ॥
translation: This is the state in relation to Brahman, O Partha; having attained to this he is not bewildered. Having continued in this state to the very last moment, he goes to Brahman that has no (perishable) body.
itrans: eShA brAhmI sthitiH pArtha nainAM prApya vimuhyati . sthitvAsyAmantakAle.api brahmanirvANamR^ichChati .. 2-72 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन । तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥ ३-१ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: If, in Thy judgement, knowledge is superior to action, O' Janardana, why dost Thou, O Kesava (still) urge me on
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . jyAyasI chetkarmaNaste matA buddhirjanArdana . tatki.n karmaNi ghore mA.n niyojayasi keshava .. 3-1 ..

sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥ ३-२ ॥
translation: With these simply perplexing words thou seemest to confuse my understanding; therefore, tell me with certainty that one thing by which may reach the highest good. V. Perplexing words: --Statements now in praise of action, now of knowledge; or something declaring Svarga as the fruit of this terrible action, sometimes knowledge as its fruit. With such words calculated to bewilder me it doubt, Thou makest my judgement vacillate. If men haunted by desires (ambition) should go to Svarga by fighting and if by the same 'act those destitute of desires should attain knowledge, still it is fit that I should be put in the way of the ascetic, but not asked to try the optional course of blood-shed and cruelty, so that I way surely up the highest good. The appellation Janadarna in verse (1) according to the Puranic Nirukti means one who has no birth and puts an end to the birth of other beings." So, It is an appropriate address in the present context.
itrans: vyAmishreNeva vAkyena buddhiM mohayasIva me . tadekaM vada nishchitya yena shreyo.ahamApnuyAm .. 3-2 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ । ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥ ३-३ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: In this world the attainment of eternal nature is of two-fold description, as I before said, O sinless one, by means of knowledge for the Sankhyas, by means of action for the yogis.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . loke.asmin dvividhA niShThA purA proktA mayAnagha . j~nAnayogena sA~NkhyAnA.n karmayogena yoginAm .. 3-3 ..

sanskrit: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥ ३-४ ॥
translation: It cannot be that from the omission of duties the person attains release called Naishkarmya; nor by mere renunciation does he attain the accomplishment.
itrans: na karmaNAmanArambhAnnaiShkarmyaM puruSho.ashnute . na cha sa.nnyasanAdeva siddhi.n samadhigachChati .. 3-4 ..

sanskrit: न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥ ३-५ ॥
translation: Indeed, nobody can ever remain for a moment without doing some work; for by everyone under the power of the Lord, by the qualities of Prakriti some work is caused to be done.
itrans: na hi kashchitkShaNamapi jAtu tiShThatyakarmakR^it . kAryate hyavashaH karma sarvaH prakR^itijairguNaiH .. 3-5 ..

sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥ ३-६ ॥
translation: He who controlling the organs of action remains thinking in the mind of the objects of sense, -he is entirely in a delusion and is called a hypocrite.
itrans: karmendriyANi sa.nyamya ya Aste manasA smaran . indriyArthAnvimUDhAtmA mithyAchAraH sa uchyate .. 3-6 ..

sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥ ३-७ ॥
translation: But he excels, O, Arjuna, who having controlled the senses by the mind begins without any attachment to tread the path of action with the organs of action.
itrans: yastvindriyANi manasA niyamyArabhate.arjuna . karmendriyaiH karmayogamasaktaH sa vishiShyate .. 3-7 ..

sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥ ३-८ ॥
translation: Do thou the appointed duty; for to do is better than not to do; and, even to keep body and soul together may not be possible for thee not-working.
itrans: niyata.n kuru karma tvaM karma jyAyo hyakarmaNaH . sharIrayAtrApi cha te na prasid.hdhyedakarmaNaH .. 3-8 ..

sanskrit: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः । तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥ ३-९ ॥
translation: In relation to action other than what is intended for Yagna, this world is bound by Karma; (therefore), Kunti's son, do thou free from attachment
itrans: yaj~nArthAtkarmaNo.anyatra loko.aya.n karmabandhanaH . tadartha.n karma kaunteya muktasa~NgaH samAchara .. 3-9 ..

sanskrit: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः । अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥ ३-१० ॥
translation: कथमिष्टकामदोग्धृत्वं यज्ञस्येत्यत आह ॥ देवानिति । हे प्रजाः अनेन यज्ञेन यूयं देवान् भावयत । सम्भावयत, हविर्भिः तर्पयत । ते हविरादिभिस्तृप्ता देवा वो युष्मान् भावयन्तु । इष्टकामदानेन तर्पयन्तु । एवमन्योन्यं भावयन्तो देवाश्च यूयं च परं श्रेयो मोक्षाख्यमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ३.११॥ एतदेव स्पष्ट (यन्) यितुं कर्माकरणे दोषमाह ॥ इष्टानिति । यज्ञैर्भाविता देवा वो युष्मभ्यं इष्टान् भोगान्दास्यन्ति । तैदेवैर्दत्तान्नादींस्तेभ्यो यज्ञादिभिरप्रदाय यो भुङ्क्ते सः स्तेन एव चोर एव ॥ ३.१२॥ एवमयजतो विनिन्द्य यजतः स्तौति ॥ यज्ञेति । विष्णुतदितरदेवाराधनावशिष्टभोजिनः सन्तः सर्वकिल्बिशैः पापैः मुच्यन्ते । यद्वा वैष्वदेवादियज्ञावशिष्टभोजिनः सन्तः सर्वकिल्बिषैः
itrans: sahayaj~nAH prajAH sR^iShTvA purovAcha prajApatiH . anena prasaviShyadhvameSha vo.astviShTakAmadhuk .. 3-10 ..

sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ३-११ ॥
translation: V. Men should propitiate the gods with their offerings in sacrifices and the gods bless men by bestowing upon them every comfort. The highest good: Moksha or final beatitude.
itrans: devAnbhAvayatAnena te devA bhAvayantu vaH . parasparaM bhAvayantaH shreyaH paramavApsyatha .. 3-11 ..

sanskrit: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥ ३-१२ ॥
itrans: iShTAnbhogAnhi vo devA dAsyante yaj~nabhAvitAH . tairdattAnapradAyaibhyo yo bhu~Nkte stena eva saH .. 3-12 ..

sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ ३-१३ ॥
translation: "The righteous who eat what is left after sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those impious (beings) only eat sin who dress food for their own sakes."
itrans: yaj~nashiShTAshinaH santo muchyante sarvakilbiShaiH . bhu~njate te tvaghaM pApA ye pachantyAtmakAraNAt .. 3-13 ..

sanskrit: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ ३-१४ ॥
translation: From food proceed the beings; from Parjanya issues food; from Yagna (sacrifice) comes forth Parjanya; and Yagna is the product of duties.
itrans: annAdbhavanti bhUtAni parjanyAdannasambhavaH . yaj~nAdbhavati parjanyo yaj~naH karmasamudbhavaH .. 3-14 ..

sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ ३-१५ ॥
translation: Know thou that Karma has its source in Brahman; Brahman has its source in Letters (Akshara); [and letters issue from beings]; the all-pervading Brahman is ever established in Yagna (sacrifice).
itrans: karma brahmodbhava.n viddhi brahmAkSharasamudbhavam . tasmAtsarvagataM brahma nityaM yaj~ne pratiShThitam .. 3-15 ..

sanskrit: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ ३-१६ ॥
translation: He who does not contribute to the working of the wheel that has been thus set in motion-he is sinful of life, he rejoices in the senses, O Partha, he lives in vain.
itrans: evaM pravartita.n chakraM nAnuvartayatIha yaH . aghAyurindriyArAmo moghaM pArtha sa jIvati .. 3-16 ..

sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥ ३-१७ ॥
translation: Whereas, for him who, perfect in wisdom (immersed in meditation), may be rejoiced in Atman alone and be contented with Atman; and (fixed) in Atman alone, be full of supreme bliss. --for him there is nothing to do.
itrans: yastvAtmaratireva syAdAtmatR^iptashcha mAnavaH . Atmanyeva cha santuShTastasya kAryaM na vidyate .. 3-17 ..

sanskrit: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन । न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥ ३-१८ ॥
translation: For him there is no purpose to gain by performance, nor anything (to fear) from omission; nor is there in the midst of all beings any one that serves any purpose of his.
itrans: naiva tasya kR^itenArtho nAkR^iteneha kashchana . na chAsya sarvabhUteShu kashchidarthavyapAshrayaH .. 3-18 ..

sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥ ३-१९ ॥
translation: Therefore, being free from attachment, do thou always devoutly perform the duty which ought to be done; for the person who free of attachments fulfils his duty reaches the Supreme
itrans: tasmAdasaktaH satataM kAryaM karma samAchara . asakto hyAcharankarma paramApnoti pUruShaH .. 3-19 ..

sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ ३-२० ॥
translation: Only with the performance of duties also, Janaka and others, it is well-known, attained to the wished-for end; besides, properly looking at the least to the guidance of the world, it is fit that thou dost thy duty.
itrans: karmaNaiva hi sa.nsiddhimAsthitA janakAdayaH . lokasa~NgrahamevApi sampashyankartumarhasi .. 3-20 ..

sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥ ३-२१ ॥
translation: Whatsoever a great man does, that other men also do whatsoever he respects as authority, that the world follows, (whatsoever he makes the authority for his conduct, that the world also follows).
itrans: yadyadAcharati shreShThastattadevetaro janaH . sa yatpramANaM kurute lokastadanuvartate .. 3-21 ..

sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥ ३-२२ ॥
translation: Nothing, O Partha, there is for Me to do; in the three worlds there is nothing unattained that might be attained; still, I am actually at work.
itrans: na me pArthAsti kartavyaM triShu lokeShu ki~nchana . nAnavAptamavAptavyaM varta eva cha karmaNi .. 3-22 ..

sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ ३-२३ ॥
translation: For, if I should not continue ever unwearied to work, all men, O Partha, would follow my path
itrans: yadi hyahaM na varteya.n jAtu karmaNyatandritaH . mama vartmAnuvartante manuShyAH pArtha sarvashaH .. 3-23 ..

sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् । सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥ ३-२४ ॥
translation: These worlds would perish, if I should not perform Karma; then I would be the author of confusion of castes, and I would be destroying these creatures.
itrans: utsIdeyurime lokA na kuryA.n karma chedaham . sa~Nkarasya cha kartA syAmupahanyAmimAH prajAH .. 3-24 ..

sanskrit: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत । कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसङ्ग्रहम् ॥ ३-२५ ॥
translation: Just as the ignorant full of attachments perform duties, O Bharata, so also the man of wisdom free of attachments should perform intent upon guiding the world.
itrans: saktAH karmaNyavidvA.nso yathA kurvanti bhArata . kuryAdvidvA.nstathAsaktashchikIrShurlokasa~Ngraham .. 3-25 ..

sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥ ३-२६ ॥
translation: The wise man should not bring about a change of opinion in the ignorant adhering to action; (on the other hand) he should himself practise with devotion and cause them to do all the duties. "
itrans: na buddhibheda.n janayedaj~nAnA.n karmasa~NginAm . joShayetsarvakarmANi vidvAnyuktaH samAcharan .. 3-26 ..

sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते ॥ ३-२७ ॥
translation: In respect of all actions brought about by the qualities of Prakriti, the Jiva deluded by Ahankara thinks ‘I am the doer.’
itrans: prakR^iteH kriyamANAni guNaiH karmANi sarvashaH . aha~NkAravimUDhAtmA kartAhamiti manyate .. 3-27 ..

sanskrit: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः । गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥ ३-२८ ॥
translation: Whereas be, O mighty armed, who sees the truth, of the divisions of qualities and functions, understands that qualities are in qualities and, therefore, (he) forms no attachment.
itrans: tattvavittu mahAbAho guNakarmavibhAgayoH . guNA guNeShu vartanta iti matvA na sajjate .. 3-28 ..

sanskrit: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु । तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥ ३-२९ ॥
translation: Those deluded by the qualities of Prakriti and mistaken with regard to them become strongly attached to the qualities and their own activities; he who has perfect understanding should not unsettle those dull beings of little understanding.
itrans: prakR^iterguNasammUDhAH sajjante guNakarmasu . tAnakR^itsnavido mandAnkR^itsnavinna vichAlayet .. 3-29 ..

sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥ ३-३० ॥
translation: With mind devoted to the highest Atman, loosed from desires and from the false notion of self and having securely placed all the actions in Me, do thou fight free from anxiety.
itrans: mayi sarvANi karmANi sa.nnyasyAdhyAtmachetasA . nirAshIrnirmamo bhUtvA yudhyasva vigatajvaraH .. 3-30 ..

sanskrit: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥ ३-३१ ॥
translation: Those sensible men who, full of faith, seeing no fault in it. constantly follow this teaching of mine, they too obtain release by means of actions,
itrans: ye me matamidaM nityamanutiShThanti mAnavAH . shraddhAvanto.anasUyanto muchyante te.api karmabhiH .. 3-31 ..

sanskrit: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् । सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥ ३-३२ ॥
translation: But those who find fault with this teaching of Mine and neglect it, know those to be devoid of discrimination, entirely deluded as to all knowledge and (altogether) lost.
itrans: ye tvetadabhyasUyanto nAnutiShThanti me matam . sarvaj~nAnavimUDhA.nstAnviddhi naShTAnachetasaH .. 3-32 ..

sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥ ३-३३ ॥
translation: Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings go (back) to their own nature; and what shall the restraint (of mind) avail?
itrans: sadR^isha.n cheShTate svasyAH prakR^iterj~nAnavAnapi . prakR^iti.n yAnti bhUtAni nigrahaH kiM kariShyati .. 3-33 ..

sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥ ३-३४ ॥
translation: With reference to the object of every sense, Like and Dislike necessarily rise up; one should not come under the power of both these; for they are his obstructors.
itrans: indriyasyendriyasyArthe rAgadveShau vyavasthitau . tayorna vashamAgachChettau hyasya paripanthinau .. 3-34 ..

sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ ३-३५ ॥
translation: More meritorious is one's own duty, be it defective, than the duty of another that is well discharged better to die doing one's own duty; the duty of another brings fear.
itrans: shreyAnsvadharmo viguNaH paradharmAtsvanuShThitAt . svadharme nidhana.n shreyaH paradharmo bhayAvahaH .. 3-35 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥ ३-३६ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Then (by the by), impelled by whom does the person commit sin, unwilling though he be, O Varshneya, as if he were constrained by force (without)?
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . atha kena prayukto.ayaM pApa.n charati pUruShaH . anichChannapi vArShNeya balAdiva niyojitaH .. 3-36 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥ ३-३७ ॥
translation: 'The Blessed Lord said: It is Desire, it is anger, sprung of the quality of Rajas. He is the great consumer, the great evildoer. Know him here to be the enemy. V. It, the worst enemy or the strongest force enquired about by thee, the cause of all evil tendencies. It, desire itself; the effect is spoken of as identical with the cause, in order to bring out the radical importance of desire. The modification of the principle Rajas into anger is also due to desire. Similarly other passions too have their origin in it and they disappear when it is killed. Hence extraordinary efforts are necessary for the purpose. Is it not possible to extinguish desire by giving all that is urged for by it? The Lord in answer describes its character to show the impossibility of such a course. Great consumer: the more the gratification is offered, the more it craves for, and satisfaction is impossible. The great evildoer: it is the prolific source of all sinful dispositions and activities, Here: in respect of achieving the high purpose of man here and hereafter. To be the enemy: as prompting the individual to evil and becoming the obstacle to salvation. The presiding Spirit over Desire is called Kalaneni.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . kAma eSha krodha eSha rajoguNasamudbhavaH . mahAshano mahApApmA vid.hdhyenamiha vairiNam .. 3-37 ..

sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥ ३-३८ ॥
translation: As flame is surrounded by smoke, as a mirror is covered with dust, as an embryo is wrapped in amnion, so this is enveloped by it (desire) V. Just as fame is surrounded by smoke, so this, the highest class of souls, is somewhat beset by desire. Just as a mirror may be covered with dust, so this, the middling class is much obscured by desire. And just as the embryo is completely wrapped up in amnion, so this, the lowest class is overwhelmed by desire and lost in it. Thus, of all the three classes of Jivas, Desire more or less obstructs the knowledge in respect of the supreme and subordinate truths, as their essential aptitude and character differ. Or this may be taken to stand for (1) the Lord, (a) the inner sense (mind), (3) the soul. Now the meaning is :- Just as flame is obscured to the eye by the smoke assailing the latter, so the Lord is obscured to the soul's perception by the desire that besets the latter; just as the brilliant flame may not be seen by others, smoke interrupting their vision, so the Lord who knows and sees everything is not perceived by others bewildered by passions. Just as the mirror thickly covered with dust cannot show the image, so the inner sense or the mind when distracted by desire cannot allow him to see the Lord or his own self. Just as the embryo wrapped up in amnion is incapable of any activity, no the Jiva overwhelmed by desire is incapable of perceiving the Lord and other truths.
itrans: dhUmenAvriyate vahniryathAdarsho malena cha . yatholbenAvR^ito garbhastathA tenedamAvR^itam .. 3-38 ..

sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ ३-३९ ॥
translation: Even the knowledge of the learned man is completely obscured by this constant enemy in the form of Desire, O Kunti's son, who is hard to gratify and is never satisfied.
itrans: AvR^itaM j~nAnametena j~nAnino nityavairiNA . kAmarUpeNa kaunteya duShpUreNAnalena cha .. 3-39 ..

sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते । एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥ ३-४० ॥
translation: The senses, the mind and Thought are said to be his abode; by means of these, obstructing knowledge, he deludes the dweller in the body."
itrans: indriyANi mano buddhirasyAdhiShThAnamuchyate . etairvimohayatyeSha j~nAnamAvR^itya dehinam .. 3-40 ..

sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥ ३-४१ ॥
translation: Therefore, O Best of the Bharatas, having first restrained the senses, do thou slay him out, the evil thing; for, he is destructive of both knowledge and wisdom.
itrans: tasmAttvamindriyANyAdau niyamya bharatarShabha . pApmAnaM prajahi hyenaM j~nAnavij~nAnanAshanam .. 3-41 ..

sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥ ३-४२ ॥
translation: It is said that the senses are greater than the body; greater than the senses is the mind; greater even than the mind is Buddhi; that which is far greater than Buddhi is He.
itrans: indriyANi parANyAhurindriyebhyaH paraM manaH . manasastu parA buddhiryo buddheH paratastu saH .. 3-42 ..

sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥ ३-४३ ॥
translation: Having thus perceived Him who is higher than Buddhi and having restrained the mind by reason, O Mighty armed, slay the enemy called Desire, difficult to overcome.
itrans: evaM buddheH paraM buddhvA sa.nstabhyAtmAnamAtmanA . jahi shatruM mahAbAho kAmarUpaM durAsadam .. 3-43 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् । विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥ ४-१ ॥
translation:
This undecaying Yoga I taught to Vivasvan, Vivasvan taught it to Manu and Manu told it to Ikshvaku.
V. This Yoga: How to discharge one's duties, i.e., as taught in verse (III-30). It consists of Nivritta Karma, which becomes the means of attaining wisdom. The Yoga Itself is said to be undecaying, as the results (wisdom and release) are of undecaying character.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . imaM vivasvate yogaM proktavAnahamavyayam . vivasvAnmanave prAha manurikShvAkave.abravIt .. 4-1 ..

sanskrit: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः । स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥ ४-२ ॥
translation: Thus, handed on down the line, this the kings and sages (the royal sages, Nimi and others, or the forefathers of Ikshvaku, &c.,) knew; long ages rolling away, it was lost to the world, O Parantapa.
itrans: evaM paramparAprAptamimaM rAjarShayo viduH . sa kAleneha mahatA yogo naShTaH parantapa .. 4-2 ..

sanskrit: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः । भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ४-३ ॥
translation: That very Yoga of ancient times is now taught to thee by Me; for thou art My devotee and My friend indeed, this is the supreme secret.
itrans: sa evAyaM mayA te.adya yogaH proktaH purAtanaH . bhakto.asi me sakhA cheti rahasyaM hyetaduttamam .. 4-3 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः । कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४-४ ॥
translation:
Arjuna said: Later was Thy birth; earlier the birth of Vivasvân ; how should I then understand this, that Thou didst' teach (it) to him in the beginning (in times past.).
V. How: on what authority; the question here as shown in the Avatarika is about the authority or proof for the fact that the Lord and the soul are separate. Hence it is easy to see that the question is sensible: otherwise, Arjuna should be taken to have forgotten all that has been told him from the very beginning about the eternal and indestructible nature of the Lord.
A. Accordingly, the Lord who perceives the intent of the question points out that he knows everything, and the other is ignorant. Otherwise, it would have been a sufficient answer to say, "Many are the births of Mine in the past," and it would be useless to say "as well as those of thine, &c.
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . aparaM bhavato janma para.n janma vivasvataH . kathametadvijAnIyA.n tvamAdau proktavAniti .. 4-4 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन । तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ४-५ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Many are the births in the past both of Mine and of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all; thou knowest not, O Parantapa.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . bahUni me vyatItAni janmAni tava chArjuna . tAnyahaM veda sarvANi na tvaM vettha parantapa .. 4-5 ..

sanskrit: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ४-६ ॥
translation: Unborn and of undecaying essence and the Supreme Ruler of beings as I am, I stand on My Prakriti and by My own will and wisdom I appear (in the world.) V. Unborn: destitute of birth even in respect of body [Let it be noted that according to the Acharya's system the word ‘Avatara’ should not be translated by the word incarnation as may be learnt from a dictionary]. Of undecaying essence: both the essence and the essential personality (body) are of course imperishable. Whence is the birth in that case? Prakriti: means bodies which are affected out of Prakriti (matter). I stand &c. I enter into the material bodies of Vasudeva and others and manifest Myself to the world. Hence the world mistakes Me for one born in the usual way. Or I Surround Myself with the material gloom under My control, so that the people mistake Me as born with a perishable body, Why should the Lord create such bodies as of Vasudeva, &c., out of Prakriti under His control and enter into them? The answer is, I stand, &c.", i.e., I follow My own nature, without any ulterior purpose, in manifesting Myself to the world.' Thus the birth of the Lord being of a quite different description from that of the Jiva, the Lord, it is clear, is truly the worshipped and the absolute Ruler, while the Jiva is separate from him and is His humble worshipper.
itrans: ajo.api sannavyayAtmA bhUtAnAmIshvaro.api san . prakR^iti.n svAmadhiShThAya sambhavAmyAtmamAyayA .. 4-6 ..

sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ ४-७ ॥
itrans: yadA yadA hi dharmasya glAnirbhavati bhArata . abhyutthAnamadharmasya tadAtmAnaM sR^ijAmyaham .. 4-7 ..

sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ ४-८ ॥
translation: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the evil-doers and for the purpose of firmly establishing Dharma I appear in every yuga (age).
itrans: paritrANAya sAdhUnA.n vinAshAya cha duShkR^itAm . dharmasa.nsthApanArthAya sambhavAmi yuge yuge .. 4-8 ..

sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥ ४-९ ॥
translation: He who thus truly understands the divine birth and action of Mine, does not on casting away this body again come into birth; he comes to Me, Arjuna.
itrans: janma karma cha me divyamevaM yo vetti tattvataH . tyaktvA dehaM punarjanma naiti mAmeti so.arjuna .. 4-9 ..

sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥ ४-१० ॥
translation: Freed from affection, (hope), fear and anger, having seen Me, the Supreme, and sought Me as the asylum, many have become pure with penance of knowledge and attained to the state of being with Me.
itrans: vItarAgabhayakrodhA manmayA mAmupAshritAH . bahavo j~nAnatapasA pUtA madbhAvamAgatAH .. 4-10 ..

sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ ४-११ ॥
translation: As they resort to Me, so do I serve them; Oh, Partha, men are all following the path of Mine.
itrans: ye yathA mAM prapadyante tA.nstathaiva bhajAmyaham . mama vartmAnuvartante manuShyAH pArtha sarvashaH .. 4-11 ..

sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः । क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥ ४-१२ ॥
translation: V. The wise devoted to the Lord worship Him alone, knowing well that all the sacred acts have to be accepted by Him and that He is the impeller of all such acts. But the Traividyas who are devoted to the mere observance of Vedic rites do not perceive this truth; they only wish to see the fruits of their acts soon realised; and so worship the other gods. In the previous verse two things have been spoken of: (1) the authorship of all acts; (2) to be the receptacle of all acts. Or these the first cannot be attributed to the Jivas ; for, evidently they are controlled by some power beyond, and it can be attributed to the All-powerful Lord alone. But how could we understand that He enjoys all the works? The second half proceeds to answer this. The drift of the answer is: only because the Lord accepts all the acts, their fruits soon accrue to the workers. Surely any other than the absolute Lord cannot be expected to dispense them readily. As Traividyas appear to worship the other deities, how to reconcile this with the foregoing statement, all are following the path of Mine? In answer to this query the first half of this verse is to be construed as an adjectival clause qualifying all man in the latter half of the preceding verse. The meaning stands thus: All those men who in the world desirous of seeing their work accomplished propitiate the gods, ultimately offer their action to Me as required by the rules; so, they (Traividyas) are also following the path of Mine. Otherwise, they cannot so soon realise their purposes in the world.
itrans: kA~NkShantaH karmaNA.n siddhi.n yajanta iha devatAH . kShipra.n hi mAnuShe loke siddhirbhavati karmajA .. 4-12 ..

sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः । तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥ ४-१३ ॥
translation: The four castes have been created by Me, based upon the divisions of the qualities and functions. Know Me the unchanging Author of that four-fold caste, and the one who is without a maker, who is no actor.
itrans: chAturvarNyaM mayA sR^iShTa.n guNakarmavibhAgashaH . tasya kartAramapi mA.n vid.hdhyakartAramavyayam .. 4-13 ..

sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा । इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥ ४-१४ ॥
translation: Actions do not cling to Me. I have no longing for the fruits of actions; he who thoroughly thus understands Me is not bound by actions.
itrans: na mA.n karmANi limpanti na me karmaphale spR^ihA . iti mA.n yo.abhijAnAti karmabhirna sa badhyate .. 4-14 ..

sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः । कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥ ४-१५ ॥
translation: With such knowledge, duty was performed even by the ancients who sought after Moksha. Therefore, do thou perform Karma which was observed by the ancients, and which is still more ancient.
itrans: eva.n j~nAtvA kR^itaM karma pUrvairapi mumukShubhiH . kuru karmaiva tasmAttvaM pUrvaiH pUrvatara.n kR^itam .. 4-15 ..

sanskrit: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः । तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ ४-१६ ॥
translation: ‘What is Karma? What is Akarma?' With regard to those, even the wise are bewildered. Or that Karma, I will tell thee; having understood which thou shalt be liberated from what is inauspicious.
itrans: ki.n karma kimakarmeti kavayo.apyatra mohitAH . tatte karma pravakShyAmi yajj~nAtvA mokShyase.ashubhAt .. 4-16 ..

sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥ ४-१७ ॥
translation: In fact, Akarma and Vikarma should be known as distinct from Karma; Karma and Akarma from Vikarma; and Karma and Vikarma from Akarma; difficult is the understanding of Karma. V.
