Supply the ellipsis Karma and Akarma from the previous verse to construe with the terms in the ablative case. From Karma: from righteous acts From Akarma, from the omission of acts. From Vikarma, from prohibited acts. The last line is meant to impress that it is generally very difficult to know the subtle distinctions between the acts to be done and those not to be done. Or, in this verse the Lord gives actually the description of Karma as promised. Now in the original, Karmanah, etc, Vikarma + Nah, Akarma + Nah should be taken as two separate words thus: Karma Nah; To translate the verse again. In fact, it should be understood that Karma proceeds from Us (Me); Vikarma proceeds from Us (Me); and Akarma proceeds from Us (Me); hence the knowledge of Karma is difficult to gain. By this it is shown Karma is essentially under the control of the Lord and it is no independent entity or cause of anything.
itrans: karmaNo hyapi boddhavyaM boddhavya.n cha vikarmaNaH . akarmaNashcha boddhavya.n gahanA karmaNo gatiH .. 4-17 ..

sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ ४-१८ ॥
translation: In activity he who sees the absence of activity and in the absence of activity he who sees activity amongst men he is full of wisdom, he has achieved the Yoga and has performed all the duties.
itrans: karmaNyakarma yaH pashyedakarmaNi cha karma yaH . sa buddhimAnmanuShyeShu sa yuktaH kR^itsnakarmakR^it .. 4-18 ..

sanskrit: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः । ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ ४-१९ ॥
translation: Him whose activities are all begun without desire and without a definite purpose, him who has his Karma burnt up by the fire of knowledge, the wise declare him a Sage.
itrans: yasya sarve samArambhAH kAmasa~NkalpavarjitAH . j~nAnAgnidagdhakarmANa.n tamAhuH paNDitaM budhAH .. 4-19 ..

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ ४-२० ॥
translation: He who having eschewed attachment to action and its fruit is ever contented and seeks no (other). refuge, he, though ever engaged in action, (he) is verily doing nothing.
itrans: tyaktvA karmaphalAsa~Nga.n nityatR^ipto nirAshrayaH . karmaNyabhipravR^itto.api naiva ki~nchitkaroti saH .. 4-20 ..

sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४-२१ ॥
translation: He who has controlled the mind and heart becomes freed from desire and divested of all surroundings; by doing what is barely physical (Bodily) work he acquires no sin. V. Here Atma is Manas (vide Bhâshya). Who...... heart shows that only by restraint of mind it is possible to become free from desire &c. Surroundings (Parigraha): are the things to which one is attached, viz., the body, organs, &c. To be divested of them is to be divested of Abhimana for them. Physical (bodily): necessary for the maintenance of the body or brought about by the body in, the organs owing to mere physical activity without the promptings of desire, &c. He acquires no sin: he does not come into the bondage of Karma. The force of the last statement is that the concluding statement in the previous verse, "He is verily doing nothing does not mean that activity is a matter of illusion; but that he is really active, and his real activity divested of certain conditions becomes powerless to produce undesirable consequences.
itrans: nirAshIryatachittAtmA tyaktasarvaparigrahaH . shArIraM kevalaM karma kurvannApnoti kilbiSham .. 4-21 ..

sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥ ४-२२ ॥
translation: He who is satisfied with what lac gets by chance, who is beyond the pairs of opposites and free from envy, being equal in success and failure, he is not bound though he may perform.
itrans: yadR^ichChAlAbhasantuShTo dvandvAtIto vimatsaraH . samaH siddhAvasiddhau cha kR^itvApi na nibadhyate .. 4-22 ..

sanskrit: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः । यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ ४-२३ ॥
translation: Of him who loosed from attachment and become released with mind steadied by wisdom, does duties towards Yagna, of him all action melts away.
itrans: gatasa~Ngasya muktasya j~nAnAvasthitachetasaH . yaj~nAyAcharataH karma samagraM pravilIyate .. 4-23 ..

sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ ४-२४ ॥
translation: (a) He who knows that Brahman is the means, Brahman is the offering, Brahman is the fire, Brahman is the act of offering, Brahman the sacrifice together with meditation, by him alone Brahman is to be reached.
itrans: brahmArpaNaM brahma havirbrahmAgnau brahmaNA hutam . brahmaiva tena gantavyaM brahmakarmasamAdhinA .. 4-24 ..

sanskrit: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते । ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥ ४-२५ ॥
translation: Some that have obtained self-control perform the contemplation itself of the Deity as Yagna (sacrifice); some others make offerings to Yagna into the fire of Brahman by means of Yagna (sacrifice)
itrans: daivamevApare yaj~na.n yoginaH paryupAsate . brahmAgnAvapare yaj~naM yaj~nenaivopajuhvati .. 4-25 ..

sanskrit: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति । शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥ ४-२६ ॥
translation: Others offer the hearing and other senses into the fires of Restraint; still others sacrifice sound and other objects of sense into the fires of the senses.
itrans: shrotrAdInIndriyANyanye sa.nyamAgniShu juhvati . shabdAdInviShayAnanya indriyAgniShu juhvati .. 4-26 ..

sanskrit: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे । आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥ ४-२७ ॥
translation: Others again offer into the fire of Yoga called the restraint of mind, kindled by knowledge, all the activities of the organs of action and the activities of Breath (Prana).
itrans: sarvANIndriyakarmANi prANakarmANi chApare . Atmasa.nyamayogAgnau juhvati j~nAnadIpite .. 4-27 ..

sanskrit: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे । स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥ ४-२८ ॥
translation: Yet others are who perform sacrifice with substances, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of meditation, the sacrifice of studying the Vedas and of acquiring, knowledge; all who make great efforts possess self-control and fulfil difficult vows.
itrans: dravyayaj~nAstapoyaj~nA yogayaj~nAstathApare . svAdhyAyaj~nAnayaj~nAshcha yatayaH sa.nshitavratAH .. 4-28 ..

sanskrit: अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे । प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥ ४-२९ ॥
translation: Some others again who are devoted to controlling the breath, having checked the courses of Prana and Apana, make Prana enter into Apana and Apana into Prana.
itrans: apAne juhvati prANaM prANe.apAnaM tathApare . prANApAnagatI rud.hdhvA prANAyAmaparAyaNAH .. 4-29 ..

sanskrit: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति । सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥ ४-३० ॥
translation:
Others, having regulated their food, sacrifice the senses into the senses. All those without exception have known Yagna, have their sins reduced by Yagna.
V. Sacrifice the senses etc : restrain and limit the activities or the functions of the senses in themselves; for, this is possible when regulation in respect of food reduces the strength of the organs of sense and of action. Or sacrifice, etc., may meal to contemplate the deities presiding over the organs, speech, etc., as being tinder the control of still superior deities presiding over mind, etc. In this case, Regulation of food is to be taken as a separate Yagna or sacrifice.
Next, the Lord points out the difference between those who obtain the knowledge of such Yagnas or sacrifices and practise them and those who do not.
itrans: apare niyatAhArAH prANAnprANeShu juhvati . sarve.apyete yaj~navido yaj~nakShapitakalmaShAH .. 4-30 ..

sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् । नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥ ४-३१ ॥
translation: Those who eat of the Amrita remains of what has been offered (to the gods) in sacrifice, reach the eternal Brahman. But, for the non-sacrificer this world does not exist, Oh the best of the Kurus, much less the other.
itrans: yaj~nashiShTAmR^itabhujo yAnti brahma sanAtanam . nAyaM loko.astyayaj~nasya kuto.anyaH kurusattama .. 4-31 ..

sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे । कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ४-३२ ॥
translation: Thus, of many kinds are the sacrifices, in detail all offered to Brahman (lit. spread out in the face of Brahman); know them all as resulting from action; having thus understood, thou seekest release.
itrans: evaM bahuvidhA yaj~nA vitatA brahmaNo mukhe . karmajAnviddhi tAnsarvAnevaM j~nAtvA vimokShyase .. 4-32 ..

sanskrit: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप । सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥ ४-३३ ॥
translation: Better than the sacrifice of substances is the sacrifice of wisdom, O Parantapa; every act, be it the smallest, O Partha, finds its accomplishment in wisdom.
itrans: shreyAndravyamayAdyaj~nAjj~nAnayaj~naH parantapa . sarva.n karmAkhilaM pArtha j~nAne parisamApyate .. 4-33 ..

sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ ४-३४ ॥
translation: Therefore, by supplication, by service, by respectful inquiry, the wise that see the truth will impart thee knowledge; do thou learn that from them.
itrans: tadviddhi praNipAtena pariprashnena sevayA . upadekShyanti te j~nAnaM j~nAninastattvadarshinaH .. 4-34 ..

sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव । येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥ ४-३५॥  var  अशेषाणिअपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ४-३६ ॥
translation: Having gained the knowledge (to be imparted to thee) thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pandava. Hence, by that knowledge thou shalt see all beings without exception in Me, the Atman.
itrans: yajj~nAtvA na punarmohamevaM yAsyasi pANDava . yena bhUtAnyasheSheNa drakShyasyAtmanyatho mayi .. 4-35.. ## var ## asheShANiapi chedasi pApebhyaH sarvebhyaH pApakR^ittamaH . sarva.n j~nAnaplavenaiva vR^ijinaM santariShyasi .. 4-36 ..

sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ४-३६ ॥
translation: Even if thou be the worst sinner of all sinners, thou shalt cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom alone.
itrans: api chedasi pApebhyaH sarvebhyaH pApakR^ittamaH . sarva.n j~nAnaplavenaiva vR^ijinaM santariShyasi .. 4-36 ..

sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ४-३७ ॥
translation: Just as fire flaming forth reduces all fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes (to nothing).
itrans: yathaidhA.nsi samiddho.agnirbhasmasAtkurute.arjuna . j~nAnAgniH sarvakarmANi bhasmasAtkurute tathA .. 4-37 ..

sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ४-३८ ॥
translation: In the world, there is verily no purifier like wisdom; and that (wisdom), he who is accomplished as to means attains in Atman in the long run.
itrans: na hi j~nAnena sadR^ishaM pavitramiha vidyate . tatsvayaM yogasa.nsiddhaH kAlenAtmani vindati .. 4-38 ..

sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ४-३९ ॥
translation: He who is full of faith and is devoted to Me alone and has mastery over his senses, obtains wisdom, and ere long thereafter attains Moksha (supreme bliss.)
itrans: shraddhAvA.Nllabhate j~nAnaM tatparaH sa.nyatendriyaH . j~nAnaM labdhvA parAM shAntimachireNAdhigachChati .. 4-39 ..

sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥ ४-४० ॥
translation: He perishes who is ignorant and is destitute of faith and full of doubt; for him who is doubting, there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness.
itrans: aj~nashchAshraddadhAnashcha sa.nshayAtmA vinashyati . nAyaM loko.asti na paro na sukhaM sa.nshayAtmanaH .. 4-40 ..

sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥ ४-४१ ॥
translation: Him whose heart is set on the Lord and actions are offered to Him, whose doubts are dispelled (lit. cut) by wisdom, whose master is the Supreme Lord, him actions do not bind, O Dhananjaya, (i.e., he attains release)
itrans: yogasa.nnyastakarmANaM j~nAnasa~nChinnasa.nshayam . AtmavantaM na karmANi nibadhnanti dhana~njaya .. 4-41 ..

sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४-४२ ॥
translation:
Therefore, having cut asunder with the sword of wisdom this doubt that has arisen out of ignorance and abides in the heart, follow the Yoga, do thou stand up, O Bharata.
V. Therefore: the results of observing or neglecting the means of knowledge, being productive of different consequences as explained above yoga: the means of wisdom which is the discharging of duties.
itrans: tasmAdaj~nAnasambhUtaM hR^itstha.n j~nAnAsinAtmanaH . ChittvainaM sa.nshayaM yogamAtiShThottiShTha bhArata .. 4-42 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि । यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥ ५-१ ॥
translation:
Arjuna said: Thou speakest, O Krishna, now of the Sanyasa of actions and now again of Yoga. Whichever is better of these two, that one please conclusively tell me.
V. In verses 22 &c. of the foregoing chapter, the Sanyasa or renunciation of desire &c. has been spoken of. In verses 15 &c., the yoga or performance of duties with devotion has been enjoined. Of these two of given description, viz., Renunciation and Performance, Whichever is better: whichever is more efficacious. That one: either Renunciation or Performance may be conclusively pointed out to me. If renunciation is of greater efficacy, I shall adopt that alone. For, it would be unwise on the contrary to follow the course of performance the performances of the bloody duties of war under the influence of love, hate, anger and other passions--a course contrary to the highest purpose to be realised.
This question of Arjuna may also be seen to arise in another way. The Renunciation of actions spoken of in verse 4. &c., might seem to refer to the ascetic life and the Injunction in 42 to follow Yoga or the course of Performance to refer to the householder's life, for the ascetics appear to be eligible for the pursuit of knowledge alone, being free from the necessity of all action, while the house holders seem eligible only for action and not for knowledge. Thus, Renunciation and Performance could not at the same time be required of the same person. Hence the question, which is the preferable course?
Now the phrase 'Sanyasa of actions,’ is to be taken as describing the ascetic life spoken of in verse 41, of the preceding chapter, The term yoga indicates the house-holder's life.
Taking either interpretation, it is clearly seen that this chapter depends on the Fourth for the evolution of its subject matter, as suggesting the question put by Arjuna; so, it is properly the Fifth in order.
A. Sanyasa does not here mean the abandoning of all duties, nor does Yoga mean the Performance of all. Therefore, the question as to the preferableness of this or that does not appear very sensible. The terms respectively mean 'freedom from attachments &. c., and the observance of duties for their own sake. Both these are possible to find in one and the same person and are necessary for the attainment of Happiness This makes the question more clearly ill-considered and useless. But, if the question, however, is merely an inquiry for information, the Lord answers it by stating that the Yoga or Performance is the best course.
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . sa.nnyAsaM karmaNA.n kR^iShNa punaryoga.n cha sha.nsasi . yachChreya etayorekaM tanme brUhi sunishchitam .. 5-1 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ ५-२ ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and Performance of duties both yield Heaven; but of these two, Performance of duties excels Renunciation in respect of duties.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . sa.nnyAsaH karmayogashcha niHshreyasakarAvubhau . tayostu karmasa.nnyAsAtkarmayogo vishiShyate .. 5-2 ..

sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ५-३ ॥
translation: He is to be understood to be always a sanyâsin who neither hates nor loves; indeed. he who is free from the pairs of opposites, O Mighty-armed, is easily released from bondage.
itrans: j~neyaH sa nityasa.nnyAsI yo na dveShTi na kA~NkShati . nirdvandvo hi mahAbAho sukhaM bandhAtpramuchyate .. 5-3 ..

sanskrit: साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः । एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥ ५-४ ॥
translation: Sankhya and Yoga are, the young say, separate (from each other), but not the wise; he who properly observes (or follows) even one obtains the fruit of both.
itrans: sA~Nkhyayogau pR^ithagbAlAH pravadanti na paNDitAH . ekamapyAsthitaH samyagubhayorvindate phalam .. 5-4 ..

sanskrit: यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते । एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ ५-५ ॥
translation: Because the place to be reached by the Sankhyas is gained by those that follow Yoga; therefore Sankhya and Yoga are (to be united in one ; he who perceives (this) perceives (the truth).
itrans: yatsA~NkhyaiH prApyate sthAnaM tadyogairapi gamyate . ekaM sA~Nkhya.n cha yoga.n cha yaH pashyati sa pashyati .. 5-5 ..

sanskrit: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः । योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ५-६ ॥
translation: Further, Sanyasa, O Mighty-armed, is hard to realise in the absence of Yoga; the sage united to Yoga ere long reaches Brahman.
itrans: sa.nnyAsastu mahAbAho duHkhamAptumayogataH . yogayukto munirbrahma nachireNAdhigachChati .. 5-6 ..

sanskrit: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ५-७ ॥
translation: He who joined to Yoga, being of pure nature has completely subdued the mind and restrained the senses and finds that He who is the Lord of all beings is his own Lord-he is not affected though he is doing (Karma).
itrans: yogayukto vishuddhAtmA vijitAtmA jitendriyaH . sarvabhUtAtmabhUtAtmA kurvannapi na lipyate .. 5-7 ..

sanskrit: नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् । पश्यञ्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपञ्श्वसन् ॥ ५-८ ॥
itrans: naiva ki~nchitkaromIti yukto manyeta tattvavit . pashya~nshR^iNvanspR^isha~njighrannashnangachChansvapa~nshvasan .. 5-8 ..

sanskrit: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ५-९ ॥
translation: He who is in the path of Yoga and knows the truth, when he sees, hears, feels, smells, eats, walks, sleeps, breathes, talks, leaves, takes, raises the eyelids, or closes them, should consider that the senses go to their objects, and think,
itrans: pralapanvisR^ijangR^ihNannunmiShannimiShannapi . indriyANIndriyArtheShu vartanta iti dhArayan .. 5-9 ..

sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ ५-१० ॥
translation: He who having renounced attachment and placed his actions in Brahman does them--he is not affected (touched) by evil, just as the lotus-leaf by water.
itrans: brahmaNyAdhAya karmANi sa~Nga.n tyaktvA karoti yaH . lipyate na sa pApena padmapatramivAmbhasA .. 5-10 ..

sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये ॥ ५-११ ॥
translation: By means of the body, mind and reason, by the pure senses, Yogis too do perform duties free from attachment for the purification of the Atman (mind).
itrans: kAyena manasA bud.hdhyA kevalairindriyairapi . yoginaH karma kurvanti sa~Nga.n tyaktvAtmashuddhaye .. 5-11 ..

sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ ५-१२ ॥
translation:
He who abandoning the fruit of action follows Yoga obtains the natural peace. He who destitute of Yoga is by force of desire attached to the result is bound down.
V. Abandoning......action: of course, abandoning also desire, wish, thought, &c., of the fruit, i.e., becoming a Sanyasin as explained above. Follow's Yoga: performs duties regarding them acts of worship of the Lord, Natural: essential. Peace: the essential blessedness to which the soul is restored. He....desire: he who has not become a Sanyasin in the above sense, i.e., does not perform duties without motives or desires and simply for the Lord's grace. To the result: to the limited consequences of action, Is bound down: is subject to endless sufferings of birth and death
A. The Sanyasa has been (verse 8) explained as renouncing Abhimana with regard to the soul’s being an agent, by himself. Now the sense of the term is extended by stating that Sanyasa consists also in renouncing the Abhimana of thinking himself to be the director of another agent.
itrans: yuktaH karmaphalaM tyaktvA shAntimApnoti naiShThikIm . ayuktaH kAmakAreNa phale sakto nibadhyate .. 5-12 ..

sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी । नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥ ५-१३ ॥
translation: Having renounced by the mind all the actions, the dweller in the body who has control over the senses remains happy in the city of nine gates, neither doing nor causing (anybody else) to do.
itrans: sarvakarmANi manasA sa.nnyasyAste sukhaM vashI . navadvAre pure dehI naiva kurvanna kArayan .. 5-13 ..

sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः । न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥ ५-१४ ॥
translation: The powerful one does not confer on the world the agentship; nor does actions, nor causes the coming by of the fruits of action; but the self-existent goes on.
itrans: na kartR^itva.n na karmANi lokasya sR^ijati prabhuH . na karmaphalasa.nyogaM svabhAvastu pravartate .. 5-14 ..

sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥ ५-१५ ॥
translation: The powerful One comes by neither the evil nor the good of another (anybody); wisdom is enveloped by Nescience; and hereby the beings have lost their understanding. V. As before, the verse has a double interpretation by taking Vibhu to mean the Jiva or the Lord. The powerful One, i.e., the Jiva who is powerful over the unintelligent matter." He cannot of his own accord accept or share in the evil work of another sinful being nor can he share in another's righteous work. So, in respect of activity or the merit of action he is not free. The verse clears the doubt that the Lord being the absolute actor might be subject to the consequences of all activity. (Vibhuh), the powerful One is the absolute Lord. Since He is absolute, He does not accept the evil arising from any action, nor the merit, i.e., the Lord is not affected by the consequences of any activity or action. If there is a ruler who is everywhere and is absolutely a free agent and doer of all, how is it that He is not seen by anybody? The latter half answer the question. Hereby: on account of the power of understanding being obstructed by nescience, the Jivas do not know or see Him.
itrans: nAdatte kasyachitpApaM na chaiva sukR^itaM vibhuH . aj~nAnenAvR^itaM j~nAnaM tena muhyanti jantavaH .. 5-15 ..

sanskrit: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः । तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥ ५-१६ ॥
translation: However, to them of whom that Nescience is destroyed by the knowledge of Atman the (Lord) to them alone wisdom like the sun shows that Supreme (Thing).
itrans: j~nAnena tu tadaj~nAnaM yeShA.n nAshitamAtmanaH . teShAmAdityavajj~nAnaM prakAshayati tatparam .. 5-16 ..

sanskrit: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः । गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥ ५-१७ ॥
translation:
Those whose thought is on Him, to whom He is the Lord, who stand firm in Him, and for whom He is the highest goal—those absolved of all sins by force of wisdom attain to the state of Non-return.
V. The direct realisation of the Supreme Being does not result from the knowledge derived from studying or thinking but once; on the other hand the constant enhancing and intensifying of such knowledge is necessary for the purpose, as discussed and established in the Sutras I-12 of the fourth Adhyaya. They should constantly think of Him till Release from the body comes, and contemplate Him to be their Maker and Ruler in all respects they should stand firm in their faith in Him; they should seek Him as their only and supreme goal. By such a devotion they see the Lord directly. The sight drives away all their sins and they attain to Heaven or Mukti from which they do not return to the Mundane bondage (Samsâra).
A. The following is intended to explain that it is necessary for direct realisation of Brahman to see all the forms of the Supreme Lord to be everywhere equal and the same.
itrans: tad.hbuddhayastadAtmAnastanniShThAstatparAyaNAH . gachChantyapunarAvR^itti.n j~nAnanirdhUtakalmaShAH .. 5-17 ..

sanskrit: विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥ ५-१८ ॥
translation: In the Brahmin who possesses complete knowledge and great humility, in the cow, in the elephant, in the dog, and in the outcaste, the learned are seers of the Equal.
itrans: vidyAvinayasampanne brAhmaNe gavi hastini . shuni chaiva shvapAke cha paNDitAH samadarshinaH .. 5-18 ..

sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद् ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥ ५-१९ ॥
translation: Even here creation is conquered by them whose mind is set on (this) equality; for Brahman destitute of defects is the equal; thus, they stand on Brahman.
itrans: ihaiva tairjitaH sargo yeShA.n sAmye sthitaM manaH . nirdoShaM hi samaM brahma tasmAd brahmaNi te sthitAH .. 5-19 ..

sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥ ५-२० ॥
translation: With settled thought, free from delusion, knowing Brahman and standing on Brahman, one should not be filled with exultation on coming by what is favourable, nor become agitated on coming by what is unfavourable.
itrans: na prahR^iShyetpriyaM prApya nodvijetprApya chApriyam . sthirabuddhirasammUDho brahmavid brahmaNi sthitaH .. 5-20 ..

sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥ ५-२१ ॥
translation: What blessedness he feels in his self whose mind is not entangled in the external contacts; he enjoys that blessedness as imperishable when his mind is given to the Yoga (meditation) on Brahman.
itrans: bAhyasparsheShvasaktAtmA vindatyAtmani yatsukham . sa brahmayogayuktAtmA sukhamakShayamashnute .. 5-21 ..

sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥ ५-२२ ॥
translation: For, whatever enjoyments or pleasures result from the contact of objects, they are all simply the source of misery: (for), these have a beginning and an end; Oh Kunti's son, the wise man does not take delight in them.
itrans: ye hi sa.nsparshajA bhogA duHkhayonaya eva te . AdyantavantaH kaunteya na teShu ramate budhaH .. 5-22 ..

sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥ ५-२३ ॥
translation: He who, while here alone, is, before leaving the body, able to beat up against the perturbation that arises from love or hate, --he has Yoga, he is the happy man.
itrans: shaknotIhaiva yaH soDhuM prAksharIravimokShaNAt . kAmakrodhodbhavaM vegaM sa yuktaH sa sukhI naraH .. 5-23 ..

sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥ ५-२४ ॥
translation: He who has happiness (is happy) within, who has delight (is rejoiced) within, and who has the Light only within, -he, the Yogi, having taken his stand on Brahman goes to Brahman that has no body.
itrans: yo.antaHsukho.antarArAmastathAntarjyotireva yaH . sa yogI brahmanirvANaM brahmabhUto.adhigachChati .. 5-24 ..

sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ ५-२५ ॥
translation: Cutting away from doubt and misapprehension, with the mind extended and controlled and bent upon (seeking) the good of all beings, the wise who are absolved of sins perceive Brahman, the bodiless
itrans: labhante brahmanirvANamR^iShayaH kShINakalmaShAH . ChinnadvaidhA yatAtmAnaH sarvabhUtahite ratAH .. 5-25 ..

sanskrit: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् । अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥ ५-२६ ॥
translation: For those who are free from love and hate, who are striving for it and have restrained the mind and have known the Atman, the bodiless Brahman is everywhere.
itrans: kAmakrodhaviyuktAnA.n yatInA.n yatachetasAm . abhito brahmanirvANaM vartate viditAtmanAm .. 5-26 ..

sanskrit: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः । प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥ ५-२७ ॥
translation: Having made the external contacts purely external and fixed the sight only between the brows and having balanced Prana and Apana that are passing through the nostrils.
itrans: sparshAnkR^itvA bahirbAhyA.nshchakShushchaivAntare bhruvoH . prANApAnau samau kR^itvA nAsAbhyantarachAriNau .. 5-27 ..

sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥ ५-२८ ॥
translation: The contemplatist who intent upon release has controlled his mind and reason and the other senses and who is always free from desire, fear and anger, is certainly the released one.
itrans: yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokShaparAyaNaH . vigatechChAbhayakrodho yaH sadA mukta eva saH .. 5-28 ..

sanskrit: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥ ५-२९ ॥
translation: Having known Me to be the one to whom all sacrifices and austerities are intended, the One great Ruler of all the world, the one Benefactor of all beings, he finds Me, the Peace.
itrans: bhoktAraM yaj~natapasA.n sarvalokamaheshvaram . suhR^idaM sarvabhUtAnA.n j~nAtvA mA.n shAntimR^ichChati .. 5-29 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥ ६-१ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: He is both Yogin and Sanyasin who, not resorting to the fruit of action, does what should be done, but not he who is without fire and without action.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . anAshritaH karmaphalaM kArya.n karma karoti yaH . sa sa.nnyAsI cha yogI cha na niragnirna chAkriyaH .. 6-1 ..

sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥ ६-२ ॥
translation: What they call Sanyasa, know that O Pandava, to be Yoga; for no one that has not eschewed wish becomes a Yogin
itrans: yaM sa.nnyAsamiti prAhuryogaM taM viddhi pANDava . na hyasa.nnyastasa~Nkalpo yogI bhavati kashchana .. 6-2 ..

sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ ६-३ ॥
translation: In the case of the sage who would well ascend Yoga, performance of duty is said to be the means, and in the case of the same sage when he has ascended Yoga, concentration is said to be the means.
itrans: ArurukShormuneryogaM karma kAraNamuchyate . yogArUDhasya tasyaiva shamaH kAraNamuchyate .. 6-3 ..

sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥ ६-४ ॥
translation: Just when he feels no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, and completely renounces all wish and thought, then he is called one that has ascended Yoga.
itrans: yadA hi nendriyArtheShu na karmasvanuShajjate . sarvasa~Nkalpasa.nnyAsI yogArUDhastadochyate .. 6-4 ..

sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ६-५ ॥
translation:
By means of the mind one should lift up the soul, (but) should not ruin the soul; for, the mind alone is the friend of the soul; the mind alone is the soul's enemy.
A. What state of mind is friendly or inimical to the soul in any particular condition?
itrans: uddharedAtmanAtmAnaM nAtmAnamavasAdayet . Atmaiva hyAtmano bandhurAtmaiva ripurAtmanaH .. 6-5 ..

sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥ ६-६ ॥
translation: The mind is truly the friend of that soul by whom, (by means of reason), the mind is conquered; but in the case of him who has not subdued the mind, the same mind is like any other enemy on the side of the enemy.
itrans: bandhurAtmAtmanastasya yenAtmaivAtmanA jitaH . anAtmanastu shatrutve vartetAtmaiva shatruvat .. 6-6 ..

sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥ ६-७ ॥
translation: He excels whose judgement is even-handed with regard to the good-hearted, the friend, the foe, the indifferent, the middling, the hated and the related : even to the righteous and the wicked. (6 to 9.)
itrans: jitAtmanaH prashAntasya paramAtmA samAhitaH . shItoShNasukhaduHkheShu tathA mAnApamAnayoH .. 6-7 ..

sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥ ६-८ ॥
translation: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु ।
itrans: j~nAnavij~nAnatR^iptAtmA kUTastho vijitendriyaH . yukta ityuchyate yogI samaloShTAshmakA~nchanaH .. 6-8 ..

sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ ६-९ ॥
translation: Under cold or heat, pleasure or pain, honour or dishonour, he who is satisfied with the aid of knowledge and wisdom, who, having subdued the senses, unperturbed like the sky, regarding equal a lump of earth, stone and gold, practises Yoga-he is said to have attained Yoga. He excels whose judgement is even-handed with regard to the good-hearted, the friend, the foe, the indifferent, the middling, the hated and the related: even to the righteous and the wicked.
itrans: suhR^inmitrAryudAsInamadhyasthadveShyabandhuShu . sAdhuShvapi cha pApeShu samabuddhirvishiShyate .. 6-9 ..

sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥ ६-१० ॥
translation: The yogin betaking himself to a secluded place, remaining single and having controlled the mind and body, eschewed desires, and refused the charity of others, should incessantly fix the mind (on the Lord).
itrans: yogI yu~njIta satatamAtmAnaM rahasi sthitaH . ekAkI yatachittAtmA nirAshIraparigrahaH .. 6-10 ..

sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥ ६-११ ॥
translation: In some hallowed spot having for himself adopted a firm seat which is neither too high nor too low, with cloth, deerskin and Darbha-grass spread one over the other.
itrans: shuchau deshe pratiShThApya sthiramAsanamAtmanaH . nAtyuchChritaM nAtinIcha.n chailAjinakushottaram .. 6-11 ..

sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥ ६-१२ ॥
translation: On such a seat having sat down and restrained the functions of the mind and other organs and devoted the mind to the One Thing, one should practise Yoga for the purification of the mind (or the 'self). V. For..... or the self: for cleansing the mud of all passions so as to make it fit for intense devotion or for cleansing the self of all the evils of Samsâra. Practise Yoga: perform meditation. This verse in repeating the same injunctions describes the course to be followed.
itrans: tatraikAgraM manaH kR^itvA yatachittendriyakriyaH . upavishyAsane yu~njyAdyogamAtmavishuddhaye .. 6-12 ..

sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ ६-१३ ॥
translation: Holding his body, his head and neck all erect and motionless, firm in his seat), closely looking at the tip of the nose, without turning the eyes to the several directions.
itrans: samaM kAyashirogrIvaM dhArayannachalaM sthiraH . samprekShya nAsikAgraM svaM dishashchAnavalokayan .. 6-13 ..

sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥ ६-१४ ॥
translation: With the mind perfectly tranquil, without fear being firm in the vow of the Brahmachârin, having restrained the mind, thinking of Myself, thinking that I am the Supreme, he should remain meditating on Me.
itrans: prashAntAtmA vigatabhIrbrahmachArivrate sthitaH . manaH sa.nyamya machchitto yukta AsIta matparaH .. 6-14 ..

sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ ६-१५ ॥
translation: Having always thus meditated on the Lord (devoted the mind to the Lord) the follower of Yoga with perfect control over mind attains the blessed state of being in Me, of which the last step is the falling off of the body.
itrans: yu~njannevaM sadAtmAnaM yogI niyatamAnasaH . shAnti.n nirvANaparamAM matsa.nsthAmadhigachChati .. 6-15 ..

sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ ६-१६ ॥
translation: However, there is no Yoga (possible) for him who eats too much or abstains altogether from food or who sleeps much or who long keeps awake, O Arjuna.
itrans: nAtyashnatastu yogo.asti na chaikAntamanashnataH . na chAtisvapnashIlasya jAgrato naiva chArjuna .. 6-16 ..

sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य  युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ ६-१७ ॥
translation: Of him whose food and exercise are of due measure, whose labour in matters of duty is regulated, whose sleep and wakefulness are also regulated, of him the Yoga becomes capable of killing out misery
itrans: yuktAhAravihArasya  yuktacheShTasya karmasu . yuktasvapnAvabodhasya yogo bhavati duHkhahA .. 6-17 ..

sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ ६-१८ ॥
translation:
When the mind completely restrained (from other objects) stands in Atman alone and when he ceases to thirst after all the desires, he is then said to be accomplished of Yoga.
V. In Atman alone: in the Lord alone.
A. When the practice of Yoga is complete, what is the state of the man?
itrans: yadA viniyata.n chittamAtmanyevAvatiShThate . niHspR^ihaH sarvakAmebhyo yukta ityuchyate tadA .. 6-18 ..

sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ ६-१९ ॥
translation: Just as the light in a windless place does not mové,'--this is known to be the simile in the case of the Yogi who has the restraint of mind and practises yoga (contemplation) of Atman.
itrans: yathA dIpo nivAtastho ne~Ngate sopamA smR^itA . yogino yatachittasya yu~njato yogamAtmanaH .. 6-19 ..

sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ ६-२० ॥
translation: (That state) in which the mind restrained by the practice of Yoga withdraws itself (from external activities), and in which the person sees the Lord through the mind and is satisfied within himself.
itrans: yatroparamate chittaM niruddhaM yogasevayA . yatra chaivAtmanAtmAnaM pashyannAtmani tuShyati .. 6-20 ..

sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ ६-२१ ॥
translation: (That state), in which he finds that supreme happiness which is perceived in self-experience and is beyond the senses, and he does not stray from the Truth.
itrans: sukhamAtyantikaM yattad buddhigrAhyamatIndriyam . vetti yatra na chaivAyaM sthitashchalati tattvataH .. 6-21 ..

sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥ ६-२२ ॥
translation: (That state), having attained which he does not regard any other gain to be superior to it, and, being established in which he is not shaken by misery, however great it be;
itrans: yaM labdhvA chAparaM lAbhaM manyate nAdhikaM tataH . yasminsthito na duHkhena guruNApi vichAlyate .. 6-22 ..

sanskrit: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥ ६-२३ ॥
translation: That state know thou to be what is called Yoga, whence results redemption from coming into misery such Yoga is surely to be practised by one with a mind that has felt disgust (for finite objects).'
itrans: taM vidyAd duHkhasa.nyogaviyogaM yogasa.nj~nitam . sa nishchayena yoktavyo yogo.anirviNNachetasA .. 6-23 ..

sanskrit: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः । मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥ ६-२४ ॥
translation: Having completely abandoned all the enjoyments that have their origin in sankalpa, and by the mind alone having restrained the group of the senses on all sides
itrans: sa~NkalpaprabhavAnkAmA.nstyaktvA sarvAnasheShataH . manasaivendriyagrAmaM viniyamya samantataH .. 6-24 ..

sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ ६-२५ ॥
translation: He should slowly withdraw the mind (from the objects of sense), by means of Buddhi full of steadfastness; he should make the mind rest in the Lord and should not think of anything (else).
itrans: shanaiH shanairuparamed bud.hdhyA dhR^itigR^ihItayA . Atmasa.nsthaM manaH kR^itvA na ki~nchidapi chintayet .. 6-25 ..

sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ ६-२६ ॥
translation: Wherever the fickle mind wanders without being steady, from every such (object), he should restrain the mind and bring it under the control of Atman alone.
itrans: yato yato nishcharati manashcha~nchalamasthiram . tatastato niyamyaitadAtmanyeva vashaM nayet .. 6-26 ..

sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥ ६-२७ ॥
translation: Supreme bliss verily comes to this Yogi who is of perfectly tranquil mind, in whom Rajas is calmed, who firmly stands in Brahman and is free from all evil.
itrans: prashAntamanasaM hyenaM yoginaM sukhamuttamam . upaiti shAntarajasaM brahmabhUtamakalmaSham .. 6-27 ..

sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥ ६-२८ ॥
translation: The Yogi who becomes free from evil (by, thus contemplating Atman, always attains with ease the final state of blessedness of being in contact with Brahman.
itrans: yu~njannevaM sadAtmAnaM yogI vigatakalmaShaH . sukhena brahmasa.nsparshamatyantaM sukhamashnute .. 6-28 ..

sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥ ६-२९ ॥
translation: He whose mind is given to contemplation, who equally perceives the Lord in everything, sees the Lord abiding in all beings and all beings abiding in the Lord.
itrans: sarvabhUtasthamAtmAnaM sarvabhUtAni chAtmani . IkShate yogayuktAtmA sarvatra samadarshanaH .. 6-29 ..

sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ ६-३० ॥
translation: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, to him I am not lost, nor is he lost to Me. I do not disappear from his view, nor does he disappear from Mine.
itrans: yo mAM pashyati sarvatra sarva.n cha mayi pashyati . tasyAhaM na praNashyAmi sa cha me na praNashyati .. 6-30 ..

sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥ ६-३१ ॥
translation: He who turned to one thing worships Me present in all beings, he, the Yogi in whatever way he be, is still) in Me. V. Turned to one thing: being persuaded that the supreme Lord is but one everywhere. In whatever way he be: whether he treads the path of virtue or neglects it; for once the realisation of the Lord having come, final release is not withheld from him, though there may be the loss of intensity or extent of blessings in heavenly life on account of such neglect. Vide Brahma Sutras on this subject.
itrans: sarvabhUtasthitaM yo mAM bhajatyekatvamAsthitaH . sarvathA vartamAno.api sa yogI mayi vartate .. 6-31 ..

sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥ ६-३२ ॥
translation:
He who, as it is to himself, sees it, pleasure or pain, equal to everyone, O Arjuna, he the Yogi is considered the most exalted.
V. Who....equal to everyone: who sees that whatever is pleasurable or painful to himself is equally such to everyone attached to the Lord and wishes to see all the brings (God's) happy, i.e., he who bears love to God's beings like unto his own self is the foremost of the Yogis.
A. Now Arjuna doubts the usefulness of the Yoga laid down by the Lord as out being in practice.
itrans: Atmaupamyena sarvatra samaM pashyati yo.arjuna . sukhaM vA yadi vA duHkhaM sa yogI paramo mataH .. 6-32 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥ ६-३३ ॥
translation: Arjuna said. This Yoga with this notion of equality which has been described by Thee, O Madhusudana, --of this I cannot see the permanency, it being changeable (restless.).
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . yo.ayaM yogastvayA proktaH sAmyena madhusUdana . etasyAhaM na pashyAmi cha~nchalatvAtsthiti.n sthirAm .. 6-33 ..

sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद् दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ६-३४ ॥
translation: Restless indeed is the mind, O Krislina; it is rebellious, strong, and unshaken (incorrigible); I think its control is very difficult as of the wind.
itrans: cha~nchalaM hi manaH kR^iShNa pramAthi balavad dR^iDham . tasyAhaM nigrahaM manye vAyoriva suduShkaram .. 6-34 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥ ६-३५ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: Doubtless, O mighty. armed, the mind is fickle and very difficult to restrain; but, O Kaunteya, it is restrained by force of habit and by eschewing passions or attachment
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . asa.nshayaM mahAbAho mano durnigraha.n chalam . abhyAsena tu kaunteya vairAgyeNa cha gR^ihyate .. 6-35 ..

sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ६-३६ ॥
translation: That the Yoga is very difficult to be accomplished by him who has not restrained the mind, is My conclusion, but that it is possible to accomplish for him who with the restraint of the mind endeavours (after it) by this means.
itrans: asa.nyatAtmanA yogo duShprApa iti me matiH . vashyAtmanA tu yatatA shakyo.avAptumupAyataH .. 6-36 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥ ६-३७ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: He who does not exert himself, (but) has faith, and who, the mind having been disturbed from Yoga, fails of the Yoga-accomplishment--what way does he go, O Krishna.
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . ayatiH shraddhayopeto yogAchchalitamAnasaH . aprApya yogasa.nsiddhi.n kA.n gati.n kR^iShNa gachChati .. 6-37 ..

sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥ ६-३८ ॥
translation: Does he, (fallen from losing both, with nothing to stand upon, ignorant of the path leading to Brahman-does he like a cloud rent by the wind go to destruction, or does he not, O Mighty-armed?
itrans: kachchinnobhayavibhraShTashChinnAbhramiva nashyati . apratiShTho mahAbAho vimUDho brahmaNaH pathi .. 6-38 ..

sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥ ६-३९ ॥
translation: This my doubt, O Krishna, Thou wilt be pleased to completely dispel; for there is none else than Thyself that can dispel this doubt.
itrans: etanme sa.nshayaM kR^iShNa ChettumarhasyasheShataH . tvadanyaH sa.nshayasyAsya ChettA na hyupapadyate .. 6-39 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद् दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥ ६-४० ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: O Partha, neither here, nor there, does he come to destruction ; for no one that practises what is righteous, beloved, treads the path of woe.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . pArtha naiveha nAmutra vinAshastasya vidyate . na hi kalyANakR^itkashchid durgati.n tAta gachChati .. 6-40 ..

sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥ ६-४१ ॥
translation: He who has fallen from Yoga attains to the worlds of righteousness and having for long years dwelt therein is again born in the house of such as are pious and wealthy.
itrans: prApya puNyakR^itA.n lokAnuShitvA shAshvatIH samAH . shuchInA.n shrImatA.n gehe yogabhraShTo.abhijAyate .. 6-41 ..

sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥ ६-४२ ॥
translation: Or he is born only in the family of the wise Yogi; indeed this is very rare to obtain in the world, the birth which is of this description.
itrans: athavA yoginAmeva kule bhavati dhImatAm . etaddhi durlabhataraM loke janma yadIdR^isham .. 6-42 ..

sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥ ६-४३ ॥
translation: Then he obtains that mental relation (contemplation of the Lord) which he had formed in the previous life; And now he endeavours for still further accomplishment, О the delight of Kurus.
itrans: tatra taM buddhisa.nyogaM labhate paurvadehikam . yatate cha tato bhUyaH sa.nsiddhau kurunandana .. 6-43 ..

sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥ ६-४४ ॥
translation: By the same practice of the former life, in spite of himself, he is indeed drawn (towards it); he may be merely seeking to know of Yoga; even he passes beyond Sabda-Brahma.
itrans: pUrvAbhyAsena tenaiva hriyate hyavasho.api saH . jij~nAsurapi yogasya shabdabrahmAtivartate .. 6-44 ..

sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ ६-४५ ॥
translation: But endeavouring with great effort he becomes the Yogi destitute of all evil and becomes accomplished through many lives; thereupon he reaches the highest goal.
itrans: prayatnAdyatamAnastu yogI sa.nshuddhakilbiShaH . anekajanmasa.nsiddhastato yAti parAM gatim .. 6-45 ..

sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥ ६-४६ ॥
translation: The Yogi is superior to those that practise austerities; he is decidedly superior to even the learned. The Yogi is superior even to those that perform Karma (duties); therefore be thou Yogi ; O Arjuna.
itrans: tapasvibhyo.adhiko yogI j~nAnibhyo.api mato.adhikaH . karmibhyashchAdhiko yogI tasmAdyogI bhavArjuna .. 6-46 ..

sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥ ६-४७ ॥
translation: Even of all the Yogis he is considered by Me to be the foremost Yogi, who worships Me with faith, with his mind and heart centred in Me
itrans: yoginAmapi sarveShAM mad.hgatenAntarAtmanA . shraddhAvAnbhajate yo mA.n sa me yuktatamo mataH .. 6-47 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥ ७-१ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: With the mind wholly clinging to Me, O Partha, practising Yoga and dependent upon Me, listen thou to that by which thou shalt know Me entirely and without doubt.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . mayyAsaktamanAH pArtha yogaM yu~njanmadAshrayaH . asa.nshayaM samagraM mA.n yathA j~nAsyasi tachChR^iNu .. 7-1 ..

sanskrit: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः । यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥ ७-२ ॥
translation: This Gnana with Vignana I shall describe to thee leaving nothing to remain; having known which there remains nothing else here to be again known.
itrans: j~nAnaM te.ahaM savij~nAnamidaM vakShyAmyasheShataH . yajj~nAtvA neha bhUyo.anyajj~nAtavyamavashiShyate .. 7-2 ..

sanskrit: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये । यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥ ७-३ ॥
translation: Among thousands of men, there is (but) someone who strives for knowledge; even among those that strive for it [there is but one who becomes accomplished of knowledge]; even among those who are accomplished of knowledge, there is but one who knows Me as I am.
itrans: manuShyANA.n sahasreShu kashchidyatati siddhaye . yatatAmapi siddhAnA.n kashchinmA.n vetti tattvataH .. 7-3 ..

sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च । अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥ ७-४ ॥
translation: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, Ether, the Mind, Thought, and Ahankara, these indeed are the eight forms into which this, My Prakriti, is divided. V. Earth, &c., the first fire at the five Bhutas, The Mind and Thought are two other principles; so also Ahankara. This last should be taken to imply and include Mahattattva, Taking the actually enumerated forms, they are eight, Taking also the implied Mahat it becomes nine. The Lord says that Prakriti directed by Himself (the Lord) assumes the eight forms in the effected state.
itrans: bhUmirApo.analo vAyuH khaM mano buddhireva cha . aha~NkAra itIyaM me bhinnA prakR^itiraShTadhA .. 7-4 ..

sanskrit: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् । जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥ ७-५ ॥
translation: This is the inferior [Prakriti]. But as other than this, know My Prakriti who is the higher and, O Mighty-armed, remains the life [of all], by whom this world is sustained. V. The purport of this verse is also to slow what the lower and higher things are over which the Lord is the Supreme Ruler. This: that which has been just spoken of in तहे preceding verse, viz., the unintelligent Prakriti. This includes the soul also. Thus, the intelligent Prakriti and the souls form the inferior or lower order of things. But as other than this: other than the unintelligent Prakriti, etc. The other is the life of all the souls and is present in the bodies of all the souls, supporting the vital principle in them. Jivabhuta in the original means that which is the life of everything and as such remains forever. My Prakriti i.e., the Prakriti that is under My control. This also includes the finally released souls. So, the injunction is: Know Sri, and the released to be far exalted. By whom, Since the released are the images of the Lord, the last clause is added.
itrans: apareyamitastvanyAM prakR^iti.n viddhi me parAm . jIvabhUtAM mahAbAho yayedaM dhAryate jagat .. 7-5 ..

sanskrit: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय । अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥ ७-६ ॥
translation: Understand that all beings are of these sources. I am equally the origination and dissolution, the source and the end, of the whole world.
itrans: etadyonIni bhUtAni sarvANItyupadhAraya . ahaM kR^itsnasya jagataH prabhavaH pralayastathA .. 7-6 ..

sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ ७-७ ॥
translation: Than Me there is nothing else higher, O Dnananjayâ; and on Me all this stands even as a series of beads do on a string (thread).
itrans: mattaH parataraM nAnyatki~nchidasti dhana~njaya . mayi sarvamidaM protaM sUtre maNigaNA iva .. 7-7 ..

sanskrit: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः । प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥ ७-८ ॥
translation: In water I am the essence, O Kaunteya; in the sun and moon I am the lustre; in all the Vedas I am the sacred syllable; in Ether I am the sound and in men I am manliness.
itrans: raso.ahamapsu kaunteya prabhAsmi shashisUryayoH . praNavaH sarvavedeShu shabdaH khe pauruShaM nR^iShu .. 7-8 ..

sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ । जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥ ७-९ ॥
translation: And in Earth I am the pure fragrance; and in Fire I am the heat; in all beings I am the life; and in the austere I am the austerity.
itrans: puNyo gandhaH pR^ithivyA.n cha tejashchAsmi vibhAvasau . jIvanaM sarvabhUteShu tapashchAsmi tapasviShu .. 7-9 ..

sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ ७-१० ॥
translation: Partha, know me, the Eternal, as the seed of all beings; I am the Buddhi of all those that are endowed with Buddhi, I am the brilliance of all the brilliant.
itrans: bIjaM mA.n sarvabhUtAnA.n viddhi pArtha sanAtanam . buddhirbuddhimatAmasmi tejastejasvinAmaham .. 7-10 ..

sanskrit: बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ७-११ ॥
translation: And I am the strength of the strong, the strength which is destitute of Kama and Raga; in beings I am the Kama, which is not opposed to Dharma, O the foremost of the Bharata race.
itrans: balaM balavatA.n chAhaM kAmarAgavivarjitam . dharmAviruddho bhUteShu kAmo.asmi bharatarShabha .. 7-11 ..

sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ ७-१२ ॥
translation: And whatever are the products of Satva and whatever, the products of Rajas and of Tamas, know them all to be from Me; know that they are in Me; but not I in them.
itrans: ye chaiva sAttvikA bhAvA rAjasAstAmasAshcha ye . matta eveti tAnviddhi na tvahaM teShu te mayi .. 7-12 ..

sanskrit: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् । मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥ ७-१३ ॥
translation: All this world deluded by these things consisting of qualities, three (in number) does not well perceive Me to be different from these (and to be) undecaying. V. Three (in number): Apparently the construction in the original requires the adjective three to be taken along with things; but by propriety it is to be construed with Guna. By these things .....qualities : by the things which consist of the three qualities, Satya, Rajas and Tumas, out of which they are produced. The termination Maya in Gunamaya has the Tâdâtmya (=self-same) force; that is, the things are identical with Gunas or qualities. Further the phrase implies and means the qualities and their products for the material cause and its effect are not different but identical. Or the adjective three may be directly construed with things as implying the three groups of the products already spoken of as Satvika, Rajasa and Tamasa. By these things: these, viz., those that are proved by the several means of evidence. All this world: this, viz., which is other than the wise and enlightened. To be different from these; these: viz., the qualities and their modifications. Hence the Lord is undecaying even in person. This fact the world does not perceive. But the contrary is understood. Here the qualification ‘by these' is to impress the fact that all things are the effect of Gunas; for the term these refers to all that are the objects of accurate perception. How could it be said that the products of the qualities become the cause of the delusion that the glorious Lord is possessed of Gunas, or qualified? If there were any causal relation between them, it would be right to say deluded by, &c. . But this is no serious doubt. Having seen in the world that all the beings possess bodies made up of the three Gunas, one might suppose that the body, &c., of Eswara are also of such stuff, they being only the body, &c. Hence it is possible and right to say deluded by, &c. The wise understand things as they are, and to exclude them the adjective this has been used in the phrase in all this. The ignorant people for want of means cannot understand the Lord to be beyond the reach of three Gunas. On the other hand, by some false analogy and reasoning based upon it the world might derive a contrary notion.
itrans: tribhirguNamayairbhAvairebhiH sarvamida.n jagat . mohitaM nAbhijAnAti mAmebhyaH paramavyayam .. 7-13 ..

sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥ ७-१४ ॥
translation: Indeed, this divine—i.e., My—Maya who is of the qualities is hard to get over; but those who resort to Me alone get over this Maya.
itrans: daivI hyeShA guNamayI mama mAyA duratyayA . mAmeva ye prapadyante mAyAmetAM taranti te .. 7-14 ..

sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः । माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ ७-१५ ॥
translation: The worst of men, unrighteous and undiscerning, deluded by Maya and having attained to the nature of Asuras do not resort to Me.
itrans: na mA.n duShkR^itino mUDhAH prapadyante narAdhamAH . mAyayApahR^itaj~nAnA AsuraM bhAvamAshritAH .. 7-15 ..

sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥ ७-१६ ॥
translation: Of four classes are the righteous who worship Me, O Arjuna: the afflicted, the seeker after knowledge, the seeker after wealth, and the wise man, O foremost of the Bharatas.
itrans: chaturvidhA bhajante mA.n janAH sukR^itino.arjuna . Arto jij~nAsurarthArthI j~nAnI cha bharatarShabha .. 7-16 ..

sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते । प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥ ७-१७ ॥
translation: Of these, the wise man, ever steadfast and devoted to One alone, excels; for I am exceedingly dear to the wise, and he is dear to Me.
itrans: teShA.n j~nAnI nityayukta ekabhaktirvishiShyate . priyo hi j~nAnino.atyarthamahaM sa cha mama priyaH .. 7-17 ..

sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥ ७-१८ ॥
translation: Great are all these without exception, but the wise man is indeed Myself (Atman only); this is My conclusion; for having devoted his mind (to Me) towards the supreme goal he has indeed come to Me.
itrans: udArAH sarva evaite j~nAnI tvAtmaiva me matam . AsthitaH sa hi yuktAtmA mAmevAnuttamA.n gatim .. 7-18 ..

sanskrit: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते । वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥ ७-१९ ॥
translation: He who at the close of many births resorts to Me with the knowledge that Vasudeva is all, ---, such a Mahatma is very rare to find.
itrans: bahUnA.n janmanAmante j~nAnavAnmAM prapadyate . vAsudevaH sarvamiti sa mahAtmA sudurlabhaH .. 7-19 ..

sanskrit: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः । तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥ ७-२० ॥
translation: By their many and different desires, deprived of understanding practising the various vows and being governed by their own nature, they go to the other gods.
itrans: kAmaistaistairhR^itaj~nAnAH prapadyante.anyadevatAH . taM taM niyamamAsthAya prakR^ityA niyatAH svayA .. 7-20 ..

sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥ ७-२१ ॥
translation: Whoever being devoted wishes with perfect faith to worship a particular form, of such a one I maintain the same faith unshaken.
itrans: yo yo yA.n yA.n tanuM bhaktaH shraddhayArchitumichChati . tasya tasyAchalA.n shraddhA.n tAmeva vidadhAmyaham .. 7-21 ..

sanskrit: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते । लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥ ७-२२ ॥
translation: Endowed with such faith he follows the worship of That; and thence he obtains those desires which are ordained only by Me.
itrans: sa tayA shraddhayA yuktastasyArAdhanamIhate . labhate cha tataH kAmAnmayaiva vihitAnhi tAn .. 7-22 ..

sanskrit: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् । देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥ ७-२३ ॥
translation: But perishable is the fruit accruing to them who are of limited understanding; (for) to the gods they go, who worship the gods; My volaries go to Me also.
itrans: antavattu phalaM teShA.n tadbhavatyalpamedhasAm . devAndevayajo yAnti madbhaktA yAnti mAmapi .. 7-23 ..

sanskrit: अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः । परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥ ७-२४ ॥
translation: Me, the unmanifest, the senseless regard as one that has become manifest, not perceiving My entirely different nature, unchanged and unsurpassed.
itrans: avyaktaM vyaktimApannaM manyante mAmabuddhayaH . paraM bhAvamajAnanto mamAvyayamanuttamam .. 7-24 ..

sanskrit: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः । मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥ ७-२५ ॥
translation: Concealed by my supreme power and Maya I am not apparent to all; this bewildered world does not perceive Me to be the unborn and unchanged.
itrans: nAhaM prakAshaH sarvasya yogamAyAsamAvR^itaH . mUDho.ayaM nAbhijAnAti loko mAmajamavyayam .. 7-25 ..

sanskrit: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन । भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥ ७-२६ ॥
translation: I know, O Arjuna, the beings that are past and present as well as those of the future; but nobody knows Me.
itrans: vedAhaM samatItAni vartamAnAni chArjuna . bhaviShyANi cha bhUtAni mA.n tu veda na kashchana .. 7-26 ..

sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥ ७-२७ ॥
translation: By means of the delusion with regard to the pairs of opposites rising out of love and hate, O Bharata, all beings attain perverse knowledge from the time of creation, O slayer of foes.
itrans: ichChAdveShasamutthena dvandvamohena bhArata . sarvabhUtAni sammohaM sarge yAnti parantapa .. 7-27 ..

sanskrit: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् । ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥ ७-२८ ॥
translation: Those men of righteous deeds whose sin is reduced to nothing, become freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites and, being steadfast in vows, worship Me.
itrans: yeShA.n tvantagataM pApa.n janAnAM puNyakarmaNAm . te dvandvamohanirmuktA bhajante mA.n dR^iDhavratAH .. 7-28 ..

sanskrit: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये । ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥ ७-२९ ॥
translation: Those who resort to Me and endeavour after release from old age and death they know that Brahman, all the Adhyatma and all Karmas
itrans: jarAmaraNamokShAya mAmAshritya yatanti ye . te brahma tadviduH kR^itsnamadhyAtmaM karma chAkhilam .. 7-29 ..

sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः । प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥ ७-३० ॥
translation: Those who know Me together with Adhibhuta and Adhidaiva, and with Adhiyagna and also at the time of departing, -those are the persons devoting their mind (to contemplation).
itrans: sAdhibhUtAdhidaivaM mA.n sAdhiyaj~na.n cha ye viduH . prayANakAle.api cha mA.n te viduryuktachetasaH .. 7-30 ..

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । किं तद् ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम । अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥ ८-१ ॥
translation: Arjuna said: What is that Brahman, what is the Adhyatma, what is Karma, O Purushottama? And what is declared to be the Adhibhuta and what is spoken of as Adhidaiva?
itrans: arjuna uvAcha . ki.n tad brahma kimadhyAtma.n kiM karma puruShottama . adhibhUta.n cha kiM proktamadhidaivaM kimuchyate .. 8-1 ..

sanskrit: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन । प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥ ८-२ ॥
translation: Who is Adhiyagna in this body and how, o Madhusudana? And how at the hour of departing art Thou known by those that have controlled the mind?
itrans: adhiyaj~naH kathaM ko.atra dehe.asminmadhusUdana . prayANakAle cha kathaM j~neyo.asi niyatAtmabhiH .. 8-2 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते । भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥ ८-३ ॥
translation: The blessed Lord said: Brahman is the Supreme Akshara; Svabhava is called Adhyatma; what is called Karma is the grand work of creation which brings forth the souls and the material things.
itrans: shrIbhagavAnuvAcha . akSharaM brahma paramaM svabhAvo.adhyAtmamuchyate . bhUtabhAvodbhavakaro visargaH karmasa.nj~nitaH .. 8-3 ..

sanskrit: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् । अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥ ८-४ ॥
translation: Adhibhuta is the decaying product; and Adhidaivata is Purusha (the soul). In this body of the embodied ones it is I who am Adhiyagna, O the best of living beings. V. Bhuta is the soul together with the body. That which is helpful to such a soul is denoted by the term Adhibhuta. This is the perishable product of non-intelligent matter, Bhava lit. that which is produced, the gross effects of matter. Adkidaivata. Daivata are the gods; what relates to them is Adhidaivata, i.e., that which is the ruler of all the gods or that which is the foremost among the gods. It is Purushia or Jiva. Purusha lit, that which abides in the body. He is the presiding divinity over all other souls. As the case may be, He is Sankarshana or Brahma. Adhiyagna: Vide derivations supra. It may also be taken as a Bahuvrihi compound. Adhi+yagna = he by whom sacrifice is presided over, i.e., to whom the sacrifice is offered. In this body, i.c., in the corporeal body attached to souls, it is only I, the ruler of sacrifice. The qualification by the adjective this is to exclude the Lord's person which is not different from the Lord's spiritual essence. So, we cannot speak of the Lord's person as being ruled by Him as the body of other beings can be. The purport of the statement, I the Adhiyagua in this body, is that the Lord is spoken of as such on account of His being the ruler from within the body of the sacrificer, of those that accept the sacrifice, and of those that confer fruits on the votaries. The question put by Arjuna is “Who is Adhiyagna in this body?” If the phrase ‘in this body’ be omitted, the intended meaning cannot be seen; for, otherwise Adhiyagna may be taken to be Agni or any one else, who may be different one from Hari, the Adhiyagan. If this, were intended by the question, there would follow the objection of asking what is known. So, to indicate exactly which Adhiyagna is meant here, the adjunct in the body is added. The adjunct turns the attention from Agni and other well-known things connected with a sacrifice to the Supreme Ruler connected with all those that perform or accept the sacrifice and bestow fruits upon the votary.
itrans: adhibhUtaM kSharo bhAvaH puruShashchAdhidaivatam . adhiyaj~no.ahamevAtra dehe dehabhR^itA.n vara .. 8-4 ..

sanskrit: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् । यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ ८-५ ॥
translation: And he who remembering Me alone at the closing hour 'departs from the body, -he attains to the state of being in Me of this there is no doubt.
itrans: antakAle cha mAmeva smaranmuktvA kalevaram . yaH prayAti sa madbhAvaM yAti nAstyatra sa.nshayaH .. 8-5 ..

sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ ८-६ ॥
translation: Remembering whatever being at the end he casts off the body he goes to that, that alone, O Kunti's son, being prepared by the constant setting of the mind upon that thing.
itrans: yaM yaM vApi smaranbhAvaM tyajatyante kalevaram . taM tamevaiti kaunteya sadA tadbhAvabhAvitaH .. 8-6 ..

sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयः ॥ ८-७ ॥
translation: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight; having set thy mind and heart upon Me, thou shalt only come to Me; and there is no doubt.
itrans: tasmAtsarveShu kAleShu mAmanusmara yudhya cha . mayyarpitamanobuddhirmAmevaiShyasyasa.nshayaH .. 8-7 ..

sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥ ८-८ ॥
translation: With the mind furnished with the course of constant practice and not straying to any other thing, thinking upon the most exalted divine Person, he goeth to Him, O Partha.
itrans: abhyAsayogayuktena chetasA nAnyagAminA . paramaM puruShaM divya.n yAti pArthAnuchintayan .. 8-8 ..

sanskrit: कविं पुराणमनुशासितार-        मणोरणीयंसमनुस्मरेद्यः । सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप-        मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ८-९ ॥
translation: The most exalted Person, who is omniscient, destitute of beginning, the Ruler, more minute than the minute, who supports and nourishes everything, whose form or nature cannot be fully comprehended, who is brilliant like the sun and beyond darkness (Tamas)—Him whosoever contemplates.
itrans: kaviM purANamanushAsitAra-        maNoraNIya.nsamanusmaredyaH . sarvasya dhAtAramachintyarUpa-        mAdityavarNaM tamasaH parastAt .. 8-9 ..

sanskrit: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन        भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव । भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्        स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ ८-१० ॥
translation: And at the moment of departure, with the firm mind and devotion, having, mainly by the strength of yoga, made Prana enter the middle of the brows, whoever contemplates Him reaches the most exalted divine Person.
itrans: prayANakAle manasA.achalena        bhaktyA yukto yogabalena chaiva . bhruvormadhye prANamAveshya samyak.h        sa taM paraM puruShamupaiti divyam .. 8-10 ..

sanskrit: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति        विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः । यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति        तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥ ८-११ ॥
translation: The goal, which is absolutely indestructible, those versed in the Vedas declare, which the ascetics free from passions enter, desiring which they practise Brahmacharya—that goal I shall briefly describe to thee.
itrans: yadakSharaM vedavido vadanti        vishanti yadyatayo vItarAgAH . yadichChanto brahmacharya.n charanti        tatte padaM sa~NgraheNa pravakShye .. 8-11 ..

sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च । मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥ ८-१२ ॥
translation: Having closed all the gates and restrained the mind in Hrid and having fixed his life-breath in the head, and having got to perfect concentration.
itrans: sarvadvArANi sa.nyamya mano hR^idi nirudhya cha . mUrdhnyAdhAyAtmanaH prANamAsthito yogadhAraNAm .. 8-12 ..

sanskrit: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ ८-१३ ॥
translation: He who uttering the name of Brahman, the Monosyllable Aum, thinking upon Brahman, departs from the body, --he attains to the highest goal.
itrans: omityekAkSharaM brahma vyAharanmAmanusmaran . yaH prayAti tyajandehaM sa yAti paramA.n gatim .. 8-13 ..

sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥ ८-१४ ॥
translation: He who will his mind not given to other things daily and constantly thinketh upon Me—to him who daily practising the course becomes ‘Yogin’, i.e., accomplished of the means, I am easily accessible, O Partha.
itrans: ananyachetAH satataM yo mA.n smarati nityashaH . tasyAhaM sulabhaH pArtha nityayuktasya yoginaH .. 8-14 ..

sanskrit: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् । नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥ ८-१५ ॥
translation: The Mahatmas that have achieved the highest accomplishment, having (once) reached Me do not again obtain birth, the abode of misery, the impermanent state.
itrans: mAmupetya punarjanma duHkhAlayamashAshvatam . nApnuvanti mahAtmAnaH sa.nsiddhiM paramA.n gatAH .. 8-15 ..

sanskrit: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन । मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥ ८-१६ ॥
translation: The worlds beginning with the world of Brahma return again and again, Arjuna; but having reached Me, he has no birth again.
itrans: AbrahmabhuvanAllokAH punarAvartino.arjuna . mAmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate .. 8-16 ..

sanskrit: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद् ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ ८-१७ ॥
translation: The people who know the day of Brahman to be a thousand ages in extent and the night (also) a thousand ages in extent--they are the knowers of day and night.
itrans: sahasrayugaparyantamaharyad brahmaNo viduH . rAtri.n yugasahasrAntA.n te.ahorAtravido janAH .. 8-17 ..

sanskrit: अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥ ८-१८ ॥
translation: From the Unmanifest all the manifested proceed at the coming of day, at the coming of night they are withdrawn only into that called the Unmanifest.
itrans: avyaktAd vyaktayaH sarvAH prabhavantyaharAgame . rAtryAgame pralIyante tatraivAvyaktasa.nj~nake .. 8-18 ..

sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते । रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥ ८-१९ ॥
translation: The same multitude of beings, (as we observe), is born again and again, and at the coming of night, under the power of the Lord, goes to dissolution, O Partha; and it is again originated at the coming of day.
itrans: bhUtagrAmaH sa evAyaM bhUtvA bhUtvA pralIyate . rAtryAgame.avashaH pArtha prabhavatyaharAgame .. 8-19 ..

sanskrit: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः । यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥ ८-२० ॥
translation: But the Supreme, the Unmanifest, is a thing entirely different from the manifested, and He is eternal-He who does not perish when all the beings do perish.
itrans: parastasmAttu bhAvo.anyo.avyakto.avyaktAtsanAtanaH . yaH sa sarveShu bhUteShu nashyatsu na vinashyati .. 8-20 ..

sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् । यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ ८-२१ ॥
translation: The Unmanifest is therefore) called the Akshara (the Imperishable). They declare it the highest goal; (for), those who reach it return not. That is My Supreme. essence (nature).
itrans: avyakto.akShara ityuktastamAhuH paramA.n gatim . yaM prApya na nivartante taddhAma paramaM mama .. 8-21 ..

sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया । यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥ ८-२२ ॥
translation: The Supreme Person, O. Partha, in whom all beings abide, by whom all this is pervaded, is to be reached only by devotion of exceptional intensity.
itrans: puruShaH sa paraH pArtha bhaktyA labhyastvananyayA . yasyAntaHsthAni bhUtAni yena sarvamidaM tatam .. 8-22 ..

sanskrit: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः । प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥ ८-२३ ॥
translation: That time wherein the Yogis going forth do not return and that wherein they, going forth, surely return, that time I shall tell thee, O the foremost of the Bharatas.
itrans: yatra kAle tvanAvR^ittimAvR^itti.n chaiva yoginaH . prayAtA yAnti taM kAlaM vakShyAmi bharatarShabha .. 8-23 ..

sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् । तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥ ८-२४ ॥
translation: Agni (fire), Jyotis (light), daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months, the northern path on this (path) going forth the men who know Brahman attain to Brahman. V. Agni: is the deity Agni. Jyotis: is the deity called Archis. Daytime: by this is meant the deity presiding over it, together with the deity Abhijit. The bright fortnight: its presiding deity together with that of full-moon day. The Six months, etc.: the presiding deity of the period together with those of Uttarayana and Vishnu. Those wise men that regularly go by the path of which the stages are commanded by these deities attain to Brahman and do not return to birth. By proximity the period of six months in this verse is what is commonly known as Uttarayana. The Northern path: the particular conjunction of time when the sun is said to turn Northward.
itrans: agnirjyotirahaH shuklaH ShaNmAsA uttarAyaNam . tatra prayAtA gachChanti brahma brahmavido janAH .. 8-24 ..

sanskrit: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥ ८-२५ ॥
translation: Smoke, nighttime, and the dark fortnight; the six months, the Southern path; on this (road). (going forth) the yogi having reached the Jyotis of the Moon returneth.
itrans: dhUmo rAtristathA kR^iShNaH ShaNmAsA dakShiNAyanam . tatra chAndramasa.n jyotiryogI prApya nivartate .. 8-25 ..

sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते । एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः ॥ ८-२६ ॥
translation: These indeed are the bright and dark paths of the world declared eternal; by the first he attains to the non-returning state; by the other he comes back again.
itrans: shuklakR^iShNe gatI hyete jagataH shAshvate mate . ekayA yAtyanAvR^ittimanyayAvartate punaH .. 8-26 ..

sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन । तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥ ८-२७ ॥
translation: Partha, no yogi knowing these courses becomes bewildered; therefore, at all times be thou constant in Yoga, O' Arjuna.
itrans: naite sR^itI pArtha jAnanyogI muhyati kashchana . tasmAtsarveShu kAleShu yogayukto bhavArjuna .. 8-27 ..

sanskrit: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव        दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् । अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा        योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥ ८-२८ ॥
translation: Having known (realised) this, the Yogi indeed passeth all that meritorious reward which is declared for the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and charitable gifts and lie also attains to the highest and foremost place (Heaven).
itrans: vedeShu yaj~neShu tapaHsu chaiva        dAneShu yatpuNyaphalaM pradiShTam . atyeti tatsarvamidaM viditvA        yogI paraM sthAnamupaiti chAdyam .. 8-28 ..

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे । ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ ९-१ ॥
